requirements.text: rcp::avtp::StreamId shall round-trip its 48-bit MAC half and 16-bit locally-assigned suffix through to_u64()/from_u64() unchanged, and two StreamId values with different MAC halves shall compare unequal.

requirements.title: byte_bus_id is echoed unchanged on responses
requirements.text: rcp::acf::make_response shall always copy byte_bus_id and transaction_num from the request it is built from, unchanged, since byte_bus_id is unique only within the owning stream_id and a response/ack must echo it back exactly.

requirements.title: Standard request kind is unconditional ACF_ABB
requirements.text: rcp::acf::make_standard_request shall build a request using acf_msg_type ACF_ABB with rsp clear, representing the mandatory best-effort, unconditional standard request kind.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 ("A request that is meant for best effort execution shall be sent in ACF_ABB format."; §11.2.1 heading itself: "Standard request – unconditional execution of request (mandatory feature)"), TC18.txt L1204-1205

requirements.title: Four response semantic types are distinguishable
requirements.text: rcp::acf::response_kind_of shall recover Acknowledge, WriteResponse, ReadResponse, or ErrorResponse from a header built by make_response with the corresponding ResponseKind, and the four kinds shall be pairwise distinguishable from the shared header fields alone.
requirements.tc18: §11.3.1-§11.3.4 ("With evt[3:0] = 0xF the response is an acknowledge"; "With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and op = 1 the response is a write response"; "With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and op = 0 the response is a read response"; "With evt[3:0] < 0x9 and err = 1 the response is an error-response"), TC18.txt L2283-2301

requirements.title: avtp_timestamp validity is explicit, not implied by zero
requirements.text: A TSCF header with timestamp_valid false shall be distinguishable from one with a valid, zero-valued avtp_timestamp; decode_tscf_header shall preserve the timestamp_valid flag independently of the avtp_timestamp value.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 Figure 5 (tv validity-marker bit held separately from the avtp_timestamp value field; layout confirmed via the §13.6 Figure 20 ACF_ABB/TSCF worked example: "...mr rsv tv sequence_num_lsb reserved tu...AVTP Time avtp_timestamp"), TC18.txt L1120-1128,4212-4218

requirements.title: Timestamp fallback rule: TSCF preferred, then ACF_GBB, then none
requirements.text: rcp::acf::effective_timestamp shall return the TSCF avtp_timestamp when timestamp_valid is set, shall fall back to a valid ACF_GBB message_timestamp when no TSCF timestamp is available, and shall return std::nullopt rather than zero when neither source is valid.

requirements.title: Decoders reject short buffers
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::decode_ntscf_header, rcp::avtp::decode_tscf_header, rcp::acf::decode_acf_abb, and rcp::acf::decode_acf_gbb shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer when given fewer bytes than their fixed-size header requires, without reading past the buffer.

requirements.title: ACF message type mismatch is rejected
requirements.text: decode_acf_abb shall return AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type when given a buffer whose acf_msg_type byte is ACF_GBB, and decode_acf_gbb shall return the same error when given a buffer whose acf_msg_type byte is ACF_ABB.

requirements.title: RELAY spec §15.5 canonical ControlFlags/Message conversion
requirements.text: rcp::acf::ControlFlags shall define FlagAck/FlagRead/FlagWrite/FlagResponse/FlagError/FlagMoreSegments at bit values 0x80/0x40/0x20/0x10/0x08/0x04 respectively, matching RELAY spec §15.5's Go definition exactly; rcp::acf::to_message/from_message shall convert between AcfMessageInfo and the RELAY spec §15.5 canonical Message shape, preserving byte_bus_id, transaction_num, read_size_or_segment, and body, and carrying message_timestamp only for the ACF_GBB encoding.

requirements.title: ServerState byte encoding
requirements.text: rcp::lifecycle::ServerState shall encode HwUnconfigured as 0x00, HwConfigured as 0x55, and RcpConfigured as 0xAA, and a freshly constructed ServerLifecycle shall report HwUnconfigured as its initial state.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 Table 36 ("svr_lifecycle_state" register: "0x00: HW_UNCONFIGURED" / "0x55: HW_CONFIGURED" / "0xAA: RCP_CONFIGURED"), TC18.txt L4388-4390

requirements.title: Forward-only, single-step state transitions
requirements.text: ServerLifecycle::advance shall accept only a request for the single next state in the HwUnconfigured -> HwConfigured -> RcpConfigured sequence, and shall return LifecycleErrc::invalid_transition without changing state for any request to skip a state, move backward, or repeat the current state.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("A request to advance the state directly to RCP_CONFIGURED will be rejected with an error response."), TC18.txt L2544

requirements.title: HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT plausibility check
requirements.text: ServerLifecycle::advance to HwConfigured shall invoke the configured HW plausibility check and return LifecycleErrc::hw_cfg_inconsistent without advancing state when that check returns false.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with HW_CFG_INCONSITENT."), TC18.txt L2545-2550

requirements.title: RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT plausibility check
requirements.text: ServerLifecycle::advance to RcpConfigured shall invoke the configured RCP plausibility check and return LifecycleErrc::rcp_cfg_inconsistent without advancing state when that check returns false.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("If not plausible the request will be rejected and an error response sent with RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT"), TC18.txt L2566-2572

requirements.title: Register-locking tied to lifecycle state
requirements.text: ServerLifecycle::generic_config_locked shall report true from HwConfigured onward, and ServerLifecycle::functional_config_locked shall report true only at RcpConfigured, with both reporting false at HwUnconfigured.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("access to the HW configuration of the RC Server shall have been concluded and as such all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked"), TC18.txt L2553-2554

requirements.title: Explicit deconfigure() backward path
requirements.text: ServerLifecycle::deconfigure shall reset state to HwUnconfigured and clear both generic_config_locked and functional_config_locked regardless of the state deconfigure was called from, after which advance shall again accept the normal forward sequence.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("it is also possible to go back to state HW_UNCONFIGURED via a write request to the server functional configuration entry svr_lifecycle_state"), TC18.txt L2574-2575

requirements.title: State-changed callback fires only on an actual state change
requirements.text: ServerLifecycle::subscribe_state_changed callbacks shall be invoked with (previous, current) exactly once for every advance() or deconfigure() call that changes state(), in registration order, and shall not be invoked for a call that fails or that leaves state() unchanged.

requirements.title: Generic vs. functional endpoint config split
requirements.text: rcp::regmap shall represent an endpoint's server-owned generic config (EndpointGenericConfig: HW pin indices, request/response queue sizes) and its endpoint-type-specific functional config (EndpointFunctionalConfig) as distinct, independently settable types.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 ("13.2 Generic part of endpoint register map (owned by the RC Server)"), TC18.txt L3932

requirements.title: EP0 whole-register-map read is unrestricted
requirements.text: Ep0::check_read_access shall return no error for any in-range target, including EP0 itself, regardless of which client is asking, and Ep0::read_whole_map shall return the current RegisterMap contents to any caller.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1 ("Via EP0 the entire register map (i.e. all endpoints) can be accessed (read and write access)."), TC18.txt L2541

requirements.title: EP0 whole-register-map write requires the root client
requirements.text: Ep0::write_whole_map shall return RegMapErrc::unauthorized_access and leave the RegisterMap unchanged when called by a client that is not the currently claimed root client (svr_root_client_index), and shall apply the write when called by the root client.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 ("Write requests to EP0 via all other streams are limited to EP0 and not beyond (i.e. other EPs)."), TC18.txt L4400-4401

requirements.title: Root-client claim is exclusive
requirements.text: Ep0::claim_root_client shall return RegMapErrc::request_rejected when a client distinct from the currently claimed root client attempts to claim the slot, shall treat the current root client re-claiming its own slot as a no-op success, and shall allow a new claim once Ep0::release_root_client has been called.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.1.2 ("The svr_root_client_index is an index that selects the request stream which is in HW_CONFIGURED still allowed to access all registers of the register map."), TC18.txt L4397-4399

requirements.title: Per-endpoint write restriction for non-root clients
requirements.text: Ep0::check_write_access (and the write_generic_config/write_functional_config calls built on it) shall permit a non-root client to write only the FUNCTIONAL config block of an endpoint it owns per Ep0::set_endpoint_owner (TC18 section 13.1 grants a non-ROOT_CLIENT write access to EP_FUNC_config only; section 13.2 places the generic block under the RC Server's ownership), shall return RegMapErrc::unauthorized_access for a non-root client writing the GENERIC config block of any endpoint including one it owns, shall return RegMapErrc::unauthorized_access for a non-root client writing either block of an endpoint it does not own, shall always permit the root client, and shall return RegMapErrc::invalid_parameter for an out-of-range endpoint id.
requirements.tc18: §13.1 ("If within the RC Server's SERVER_config the ROOT_CLIENT is configured only the ROOT_CLIENT has write access to all RC Server configuration register maps. For other RC Clients than the ROOT_CLIENT write access is only given to EP_functional configuration of endpoints which are allocated to the RC Client within the EP_ID_config register map."), TC18.txt L3914-3916

requirements.title: Config-block locks are enforced independently by EP0
requirements.text: Ep0::write_generic_config shall return RegMapErrc::locked_mem_access once ServerLifecycle::generic_config_locked is true, and Ep0::write_functional_config shall return RegMapErrc::locked_mem_access once ServerLifecycle::functional_config_locked is true, even when called by a client that REQ-REGMAP-005 would otherwise authorize for that block.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.2 ("access to the HW configuration of the RC Server shall have been concluded and as such all access to the HW_config and EP_generic_config are locked"), TC18.txt L2553-2554

requirements.title: General bootstrap register-map fields
requirements.text: RegisterMap shall hold magic, protocol_version_major/minor, vendor_id, device_id, endpoint_count, max_streams, max_queue_depth, svr_implemented_options, and a TablePointer (offset+capacity) for each of the HW pin-map, request-stream, response-stream, EP-ID mapping, and functional-config tables, all independently settable and retrievable.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.5 Table 20 ("RC Server configuration static part"), TC18.txt L2895-3050

requirements.title: HW pin-mapping config storage
requirements.text: RegisterMap::hw_pin_map shall store an ordered list of HwPinMapEntry (pin_id, function) values and return them unchanged.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.6 Table 21 ("HW_config"), TC18.txt L3077-3108

requirements.title: RequestStreamConfig carries the full v2.6.0 watchdog/safe-state register set
requirements.text: regmap::RequestStreamConfig shall carry rx_wd_timeout_interval, rx_wd_enable, rx_wd_safestate_enable, rx_wd_info_enable, rx_enforce_e2e, rx_enforce_seq, rx_seq_safestate_enable, rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable, rx_safety_measure, rx_safestate_sequencer, and rx_safe_sequencer_state as independently settable fields, each defaulting to disabled/false/RxSafetyMeasure::ForceHighImpedance.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("Request stream configuration"), TC18.txt L3217-3293

requirements.title: EP-ID/byte_bus_id mapping preserves client insertion order
requirements.text: RegisterMap::ep_id_mapping shall preserve EpIdMappingEntry values in the exact order a client inserted them, without the server re-deriving, validating, or re-sorting an ordering of its own.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.8 ("The parameters Request_Stream_Index and BBID shall occur in ascending order. This has to be ensured by the instance that is sending the configuration to this table."), TC18.txt L3364-3365

requirements.title: Response/ack queue config fields
requirements.text: ResponseQueueConfig shall provide independently settable response_queue_size and ack_queue_size fields.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.9 Table 27 ("Responder QUEUE_config"), TC18.txt L3402-3444

requirements.title: Sequencer-state registers persist independent 8-bit values
requirements.text: RegisterMap::sequencer_states shall store one persistent 8-bit SequencerState value per configured slot, each independently settable and retrievable, ahead of the sequencing behavior introduced in v2.5.0.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.10 Table 28 ("SEQUENCER_config"), TC18.txt L3460-3493

requirements.title: INVALID_PARAMETER on out-of-range register-map requests
requirements.text: Ep0::check_read_access, Ep0::check_write_access, and Ep0::set_endpoint_owner shall return RegMapErrc::invalid_parameter for a target endpoint id outside the configured endpoint_count range, or (for set_endpoint_owner) for a request to assign an owner to EP0 itself.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.6 Table 30 ("Error codes in responses"), TC18.txt L3804-3844

requirements.title: The four mandatory register-map error codes are distinct
requirements.text: rcp::regmap::RegMapErrc shall define UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS, LOCKED_MEM_ACCESS, REQUEST_REJECTED, and INVALID_PARAMETER as pairwise-distinct error codes in their own error_category, each with a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: EndpointGenericConfig's per-endpoint E2E CRC safe-mode toggles
requirements.text: regmap::EndpointGenericConfig::ep_req_crc_enable, ep_ack_crc_enable, and ep_response_crc_enable shall each default to false and shall be independently settable without affecting one another.

requirements.title: Discovery request framing — byte_bus_id 0, register-map address 0
requirements.text: rcp::discovery::make_discovery_request shall build an unconditional ACF_ABB read (op=false) targeting byte_bus_id 0 (kDiscoveryByteBusId), and kDiscoveryRegisterAddress shall be 0, fixing discovery reads at the general bootstrap/magic-number register-map region.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 Table 18 ("Byte_bus_id 00000000000b"; "op 1b (read request)"), TC18.txt L2746-2758

requirements.title: Discovery is NTSCF-only; a TSCF-headed discovery request is dropped
requirements.text: rcp::discovery::encode_discovery_request shall always produce an NTSCF-headed frame, and rcp::discovery::decode_discovery_request shall return DiscoveryErrc::tscf_headed_request_dropped without decoding further when given a frame whose AVTPDU subtype byte is TSCF.
requirements.tc18: §12.6.1 ("AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped without further response, as well as requests in ACF_GBB format."), TC18.txt L2743

requirements.title: The first discovery request claims the discovery stream
requirements.text: DiscoveryClaim::on_discovery_request shall return ClaimOutcome::Claimed and record `client` as the claim holder when no active claim currently exists and server_state is HwUnconfigured or HwConfigured.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("The first discovery request the RC server receives in HW_UNCONFIGURED or HW_CONFIGURED state is used to set the discovery stream from which now on configuration requests will be accepted."), TC18.txt L2732-2733

requirements.title: The discovery claim lapses after Discovery_TimeOut
requirements.text: DiscoveryClaim shall treat a claim as lapsed once (now - claimed_at) is at least Discovery_TimeOut (kDefaultTimeout, ~20ms by default), after which may_configure shall return false for the prior holder and a subsequent discovery request from any client shall be able to claim the stream anew.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("If the RC Server does not receive configuration requests on the stream for a certain time (Discovery_TimeOut) it will drop the discovery stream and is open for a new discovery."), TC18.txt L2733-2735

requirements.title: A claim does not block concurrent discovery reads from other clients
requirements.text: DiscoveryClaim::on_discovery_request from a client other than the active holder shall return ClaimOutcome::HeldByOther without altering the existing claim, and shall never affect whether that client's underlying discovery read is answered; the same holder re-requesting before the claim lapses shall return ClaimOutcome::AlreadyHeld.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("If multiple discovery requests are received from different RC Clients all requests are responded with the server_config map, but only the first one will be allowed as configuration stream."), TC18.txt L2735-2737

requirements.title: Only the active claim holder may issue a configuration request
requirements.text: DiscoveryClaim::on_configuration_request shall return true and consume (release) the claim only when called by the client currently holding an active, unlapsed claim; a call from any other client shall return false and shall leave an existing other-held claim untouched.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("If others send configuration requests they will be rejected and get an error response."), TC18.txt L2736-2737

requirements.title: Discovery-stream claiming is scoped to HW_UNCONFIGURED/HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: DiscoveryClaim::on_discovery_request shall return ClaimOutcome::NotEligible and leave any existing claim state unchanged whenever server_state is RcpConfigured.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.4 ("Changes in configuration via a discovery request are no longer allowed."), TC18.txt L2879-2880

requirements.title: DiscoveryErrc is a distinct error category with non-empty messages
requirements.text: rcp::discovery::make_error_code(DiscoveryErrc::tscf_headed_request_dropped) shall report rcp::discovery::discovery_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: A server answers discovery in every lifecycle state
requirements.text: rcp::discovery::should_answer_discovery shall return true for HwUnconfigured, HwConfigured, and RcpConfigured alike, reflecting the mandatory-baseline requirement that discovery is answered regardless of lifecycle state.
requirements.tc18: §12.6 ("An RC Server may receive a “discovery request” in any state of the life-cycle and shall send a “discovery response” in return."), TC18.txt L2731-2732

requirements.title: GPIO and SPI endpoint-type ids
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeGpio shall equal 0x02 and rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeSpi shall equal 0x03, matching the ep_type ids this milestone assigns for the GPIO and SPI endpoint types.

requirements.title: evt[2:0] write-semantics decode
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::write_semantics_of shall map evt_op values 0-7 to Replace/Or/And/Xor/Reserved/Add/Subtract/Reconfigure respectively, masking its argument to the low 3 bits before conversion.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row: "000b The byte_msg_payload is presented at the interface" / "001b"-"011b" OR/AND/XOR / "100b reserved" / "101b"/"110b" add/subtract / "111b" reconfigure), TC18.txt L4093-4116

requirements.title: Generic bitmask write combinators
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::apply_bitmask_write shall compute Replace/Or/And/Xor of `current` and `operand` correctly for WriteSemantics::Replace/Or/And/Xor respectively.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("The \u201cbyte_msg_payload\u201d bitwise OR/AND/XOR \u201ccurrent interface status\u201d is written to the interface"), TC18.txt L4093-4105

requirements.title: Saturating add/subtract
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::apply_bitmask_write's Add and Subtract semantics, and the underlying rcp::endpoint::saturating_add/saturating_subtract helpers, shall clamp at the representable range's max/0 respectively rather than wrapping on overflow/underflow.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 ("While doing additions and subtractions neither overflows nor wrap-arounds shall occur. The values are saturated at 0x0000 on the low side and 0xFFFF at the high side."), TC18.txt L4118-4119

requirements.title: Reserved and Reconfigure are not generic combinators
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::apply_bitmask_write shall return EndpointErrc::reserved_write_semantics for WriteSemantics::Reserved and EndpointErrc::non_combinable_write_semantics for WriteSemantics::Reconfigure, and EndpointErrc shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("100b reserved \u2013request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"; "111b The byte_msg_payload is not presented to the interface but used to change the configuration of the endpoint"), TC18.txt L4106-4115

requirements.title: Generic trigger-signal table
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::TriggerRegistry::notify shall queue a signal for drain() only when that signal id is currently enabled, disable() shall stop further notifications for that id from queuing, and drain() shall return queued signal ids in occurrence order and clear the queue.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 ("Each endpoint may generate one or more trigger signals."), TC18.txt L1689

requirements.title: evt[2:0] Row 2 (ADC/PWM_IN/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO) classification
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of shall classify evt_op values, masked to the low 3 bits first: 000b as EvtRow2Kind::Plain, 111b as EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite, and every other value (001b-110b) as EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, per TC18 §13.5 Table 33's shared rule for the {ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO} endpoint-type row. EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category. RESOLVED AMBIGUITY: Table 33's own literal text groups evt[2:0]=000b together with 001b-110b as a single "reserved -- reject" range for this row, which read in isolation would make evt=000b illegal too, leaving every endpoint type in this row permanently unusable for ordinary requests. That reading is contradicted by TC18's own §13.7.9.3 worked example for ADC (a member of this row) showing evt[2:0]=000b used in an ordinary standard read request that succeeds normally. This implementation follows the worked example (evt=000b is the ordinary, successful case), the same resolution c-RCP's rcp_acf_evt_row2_is_plain() already shipped for this identical ambiguity.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: The byte_msg_payload is not presented to the interface but used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: GPIO payload is a 4-byte big-endian bitmask
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::kGpioPayloadLen shall be 4 and kMaxPins shall be 32; encode_gpio_payload/decode_gpio_payload shall round-trip a PinMask value in big-endian byte order, and decode_gpio_payload shall return avtp::AvtpErrc::short_buffer when given fewer than kGpioPayloadLen bytes.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("A request not having exactly four bytes is rejected and an error response with error code = INVALID_PARAMETER will be sent"), TC18.txt L4799-4800

requirements.title: GPIO write semantics: generic combinators
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::apply_gpio_write shall apply Replace/Or/And/Xor to GpioState::values via rcp::endpoint::apply_bitmask_write.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("The byte_msg_payload is presented at the interface"; GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=000b-011b), TC18.txt L4093-4105

requirements.title: GPIO write semantics: saturating Add/Subtract
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::apply_gpio_write shall apply the saturating Add/Subtract rule to GpioState::values, clamping instead of wrapping, using the same rcp::endpoint saturation helpers PWM_OUT is expected to reuse at v2.4.0.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 ("While doing additions and subtractions neither overflows nor wrap-arounds shall occur. The values are saturated at 0x0000 on the low side and 0xFFFF at the high side."), TC18.txt L4118-4119

requirements.title: GPIO write semantics: Reserved rejected, Reconfigure retargets directions
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::apply_gpio_write shall return an error without modifying GpioState for WriteSemantics::Reserved, and shall replace GpioState::directions (leaving GpioState::values unchanged) for WriteSemantics::Reconfigure.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=100b "reserved – request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"; evt[2:0]=111b "used to change the configuration of the endpoint"), TC18.txt L4106-4116

requirements.title: GPIO per-pin change/rising/falling trigger signals
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::evaluate_gpio_triggers shall notify a pin's Change signal on any bit transition and additionally its Rising or Falling signal depending on transition direction, reporting only signals the caller's rcp::endpoint::TriggerRegistry had armed, and shall notify nothing for a pin whose bit did not change.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.1 ("The GPIO endpoint optionally generates triggers for all its mapped IO-pins on the change, falling and rising edge."), TC18.txt L4816

requirements.title: GPIO functional config block wiring
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::encode_gpio_functional_config/decode_gpio_functional_config shall round-trip a pin-direction mask and per-pin enabled-edge bitmasks through rcp::regmap::EndpointFunctionalConfig::data, and decode_gpio_functional_config shall return avtp::AvtpErrc::short_buffer for an undersized blob.

requirements.title: GpioEndpoint request-dispatch pattern
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::GpioEndpoint::handle_write shall apply one write request's semantics and operand to its internal state, evaluate the resulting transition's trigger signals, and report the endpoint's new pin-value bitmask, in one call.

requirements.title: GpioEndpoint error propagation and GpioErrc category
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::GpioEndpoint::handle_write shall propagate an underlying write-semantics error without modifying its endpoint state, and rcp::gpio::GpioErrc shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.

requirements.title: A write to a pin configured as input leaves that pin's value unchanged
requirements.text: rcp::gpio::apply_gpio_write shall, for every non-Reconfigure write semantics, commit the write combinator's result to GpioState::values only for bit positions where GpioState::directions selects output, and shall leave GpioState::values unchanged at every bit position where directions selects input, regardless of what the request's operand or combinator result specify for that position.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.4.3 ("A write request to an input pin is ignored for this input pin"), TC18.txt L4890

requirements.title: SPI channel selection via evt[2:0]
requirements.text: rcp::spi::kMaxChannels shall be 6; rcp::spi::channel_of shall accept evt[2:0] values 0-5 as channel selectors (masking its input to the low 3 bits first) and return SpiErrc::channel_out_of_range for 6 and 7.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.2 ("up to 6 CS signals may be handled by the SPI endpoint via its configurations"; "the SPI bus functional configuration supports up to 6 different configurations in parallel. Which configuration is used within an SPI request is determined by evt[2:0]."), TC18.txt L4730-4739

requirements.title: SPI compound-wait status-byte truncation rule
requirements.text: rcp::spi::compound_wait_matches shall compare only the first kCompoundWaitCompareLen (4) bytes of a status transfer against the expected pattern, ignoring any difference beyond that window, shall reject a status transfer longer than kMaxStatusBytes (20), and shall return false when the truncated comparison window is empty.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1 ("the interface status shall be capped to the length of the byte message payload. For SPI this means that e.g. only the first four out of 20 received bytes will be checked when the byte_msg_payload in the compound wait has only four bytes."), TC18.txt L4136-4139

requirements.title: SPI raw PICO-out/POCI-in transfer
requirements.text: rcp::spi::SpiEndpoint::transfer shall record the sent and received bytes for the given channel independently of every other channel's last transfer, and shall return SpiErrc::channel_out_of_range for a channel >= kMaxChannels without recording anything.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 ("The RC Client can request the SPI endpoint to send one or more bytes that are delivered as byte_msg_payload of an ACF_ABB/GBB to the endpoint."), TC18.txt L4597-4598

requirements.title: SPI transfer-complete and per-CS trigger signals
requirements.text: rcp::spi::SpiEndpoint::transfer shall notify CsAssert, then TransferComplete, then CsDeassert for the transferred channel's rcp::endpoint::TriggerRegistry, spi_signal_id shall assign a distinct SignalId to every (channel, signal) pair, and a channel's armed signals shall not affect notification delivery for any other channel.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.3.1 Table 41 ("spi trigger outputs"; 0 = SPI execution done, 2+2n = CSn asserted, 3+2n = CSn de-asserted), TC18.txt L4603-4611

requirements.title: SpiErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::spi::make_error_code(SpiErrc::channel_out_of_range) shall report rcp::spi::spi_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: i2c_mode open item — coarse high-speed decode only
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::i2c_mode_of shall map AcfMessageInfo::hs=false to I2cMode::Standard and hs=true to I2cMode::HighSpeed, and shall not attempt to distinguish any finer I2C speed grade, per this milestone's documented open item pending a future spec errata pass.

requirements.title: I2C compound-wait arbitrary-bit-sequence match
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::compound_wait_matches_bits shall compare exactly the leading `bit_len` bits of `received` against `expected` (MSB-first within a byte, comparing only the top `bit_len % 8` bits of a partial final byte), shall return false when either buffer is shorter than `bit_len` requires, and shall return false for `bit_len == 0`.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.1 ("Optionally the Client can request the I²C endpoint to wait for a pre-defined bit sequence has been received from a connected device."), TC18.txt L5203-5204

requirements.title: I2C controller-only raw byte-stream transfer
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::I2cEndpoint::transfer shall record the exact byte sequences passed as `out_bytes` and `in_bytes` — including any address byte(s) the caller embeds in `out_bytes` — retrievable via last_sent()/last_received().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.3 ("The byte msg payload is the I2C payload including the address. The I2C endpoint does not know whether there is a 7- or 10-bit address, since the endpoint is just transparent."; Figure 30 – "i2c request format"), TC18.txt L5240-5257

requirements.title: I2C TransferComplete and Nack trigger signals
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::I2cEndpoint::transfer shall notify TransferComplete on every transfer, shall additionally notify Nack and return I2cErrc::nack when called with acked=false, and shall notify only TransferComplete for an acknowledged transfer.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.7.4 ("An I²C endpoint optionally generates HW trigger events"; Table 50's own Event column is blank in the extraction, so the concrete TransferComplete/Nack signal identities below this clause are this implementation's own, not spec-named), TC18.txt L5262-5264

requirements.title: I2cErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::make_error_code(I2cErrc::nack) shall report rcp::i2c::i2c_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: I2cEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before transferring
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::I2cEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to transfer() with out_bytes/in_bytes/acked unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without recording anything as sent or received.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: I2cEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::i2c::I2cEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported without recording anything as sent or received and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary transfer or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone. I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: UART TX queue is independent of the RX FIFO
requirements.text: rcp::uart::UartEndpoint::enqueue_tx shall append to a TX queue independent of the RX FIFO's contents, drain_tx shall return and clear exactly what was queued, and enqueue_tx shall return UartErrc::tx_queue_overflow rather than partially enqueueing when the push would exceed kTxQueueCapacity.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("These two processes are independent from each other, thus the UART EP has two EP request storages, one for transmitting data and one for receiving data."), TC18.txt L5292-5293

requirements.title: UART RX FIFO fill/drain semantics
requirements.text: rcp::uart::UartEndpoint::rx_fill shall append bytes to the RX FIFO, rx_available shall report its current occupancy, and rx_fill shall return UartErrc::rx_fifo_overflow rather than partially filling when the push would exceed kRxFifoCapacity.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("While receiving the UART EP shifts the received data into a fifo-rx-buffer that has a length of uart_rx_fifo_size. The buffer is emptied by read requests. Overflow is flagged in the UART EP status register."), TC18.txt L5294-5295

requirements.title: UART read completion: read_size reached or uart_timeout elapsed
requirements.text: rcp::uart::UartEndpoint::handle_read shall drain up to `read_size` bytes currently available in the RX FIFO, shall report out_timed_out=true only when read_size was not fully reached and elapsed_ms >= uart_timeout_ms, and shall return UartErrc::read_size_exceeds_bound for a read_size greater than kMaxReadSize without modifying the RX FIFO.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.1 ("A read request will be started as soon as the fifo-rx-buffer is filled with as many bytes as requested in the read_size or when the uart_timeout has expired"), TC18.txt L5297-5298

requirements.title: UART payload-less pure read requests
requirements.text: rcp::uart::UartEndpoint::handle_pure_read shall drain and return every byte currently buffered in the RX FIFO without waiting on read_size or uart_timeout, and shall return an empty result when the RX FIFO is empty.

requirements.title: UART sub-octet bit-width padding rules
requirements.text: rcp::uart::pack_frame_to_octet shall mask a frame's value to its low bits_per_frame bits (zero-padding the remaining high bits of the octet), rcp::uart::unpack_frame_bits shall invert that masking, and both shall return UartErrc::bits_per_frame_out_of_range for bits_per_frame outside [kMinBitsPerFrame, kMaxBitsPerFrame].
requirements.tc18: §13.7.8.3 ("In case uart_nr_bits is not a multiple integer of 8, then the RC Client might need to append up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits to create a payload in requests that fits into an integer multiple of octects. Equally the UART EP will append up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits in such cases in the responses. When transmitting the EP ignores the last up to 'uart_nr_bits - 1' bits from the request payload, when the length of the payload is not an integer multiple of uart_nr_bits."), TC18.txt L5402-5406

requirements.title: UART RX FIFO / read_size single-AVTPDU accepted limitation
requirements.text: rcp::uart::kRxFifoCapacity and rcp::uart::kTxQueueCapacity shall both equal kMaxReadSize, documenting the accepted limitation that both are bounded so a UART read response always fits one unfragmented AVTPDU, consistent with ROADMAP.md milestone 52's fragmentation no-go decision.

requirements.title: UartErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::uart::make_error_code(UartErrc::rx_fifo_overflow) shall report rcp::uart::uart_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: UartEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before routing on req.op to enqueue_tx or handle_read
requirements.text: rcp::uart::UartEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall route on its is_write argument: true delegates to enqueue_tx(tx_bytes) with the TX queue unchanged from that function's own behavior, false delegates to handle_read(read_size, elapsed_ms, uart_timeout_ms, out_data, out_timed_out) unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without invoking enqueue_tx or handle_read and without touching the TX queue or RX FIFO.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: UartEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::uart::UartEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return UartErrc::config_write_not_supported without invoking enqueue_tx or handle_read, without touching the TX queue or RX FIFO, and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary TX/RX operation or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported, ADC's AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported, PWM_IN's PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported, LIN's LinErrc::config_write_not_supported, and CAN's CanErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. UartErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: ADC arithmetic-mean averaging combinator
requirements.text: rcp::adc::compute_average shall compute the arithmetic mean of a non-empty sample set and shall return AdcErrc::no_signal for an empty sample set.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("A measured value may contain the average of multiple ADC samples depending on the ADC EP functional configuration."), TC18.txt L5580

requirements.title: ADC three-level averaging model
requirements.text: rcp::adc::AdcEndpoint::request_reading shall average adc_avg_intervals_per_request raw samples per averaged-interval value (level 1), shall combine adc_combine_avg_values such averaged-interval values into the reported result (level 2), and shall return AdcErrc::invalid_averaging_config when either configuration field is 0.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("For the readings acquired during the averaging interval given in number of samples (an implementation may decide to fix this to 1) the average is calculated. Finally, the COMBINE_NR_VAL defines how many measurement values (i.e. averaging results) will be put in one response frame."), TC18.txt L5455-5457 (correcting this entry's prior citation, which misattributed the quote to §13.7.9.2 L5040 — the quote is only found at §13.7.9.1 L5455-5457)

requirements.title: ADC request-driven sampling only
requirements.text: rcp::adc::AdcEndpoint::request_reading shall invoke its sample source exactly adc_avg_intervals_per_request * adc_combine_avg_values times per call — no more, no fewer — and shall return AdcErrc::no_signal (this endpoint's analog of PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL on the request path) the first time the sample source reports a missing capture, without free-running or pushing samples outside a call.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("The ADC only samples the input, when a request is executed. Consequently, no trigger will occur when there is no request to sample."), TC18.txt L5476-5477

requirements.title: ADC ExternalTrigger cadence pattern
requirements.text: rcp::adc::AdcEndpoint::request_reading_from_trigger_queue shall consume exactly adc_avg_intervals_per_request * adc_combine_avg_values entries from the front of the supplied trigger-sample queue, shall erase only the consumed entries on success, and shall return AdcErrc::no_signal on a queue holding fewer entries than required.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.1 ("Reading ADC values from an endpoint can be triggered e.g. by a PWM output trigger event by using a Trigger request, which triggers on the PWM EP."), TC18.txt L5446-5447

requirements.title: ADC no-signal handling for a missing triggered capture
requirements.text: rcp::adc::AdcEndpoint::request_reading_from_trigger_queue shall return AdcErrc::no_signal when a consumed queue entry is std::nullopt, without producing a result derived from that entry.

requirements.title: AdcErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::adc::make_error_code(AdcErrc::no_signal) shall report rcp::adc::adc_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: encode_adc_value encodes a single measurement as a 16-bit big-endian wire value
requirements.text: rcp::adc::encode_adc_value shall encode its uint16_t argument as exactly rcp::adc::kAdcValueLen (2) bytes, big-endian, matching the "16 bit ADC value" field TC18's ADC response figures show.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.9.3 ("16 bit ADC value 0"/"16 bit ADC value 1" fields, Figure 34/Figure 35 - ADC response with 8 measurements), TC18.txt L5590-5628

requirements.title: AdcEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before sampling
requirements.text: rcp::adc::AdcEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to request_reading() with cfg/take_sample/out_value unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without invoking take_sample or otherwise touching out_value.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: AdcEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::adc::AdcEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported without invoking take_sample or otherwise touching out_value and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary read or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: PWM_OUT/PWM_IN shared period/active-duration payload shape
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmValue shall default both period and active_duration to 0, and both rcp::pwm::PwmOutEndpoint and rcp::pwm::PwmInEndpoint shall operate on this same two-field type.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.5.3 ("The PWM_out request and response contain two values in the payload. The active time of the PWM signal as well as the period of the signal in clock ticks of the clock selected for this PWM_out endpoint."; Figure 27 – "pwmo request format"), TC18.txt L5031-5038

requirements.title: PWM_OUT write semantics: Replace applies directly
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmOutEndpoint::handle_write shall apply WriteSemantics::Replace by directly assigning `period` and `active_duration` from the request, matching one of the eight write semantics the OPEN Alliance TC18 Remote Control Protocol Specification's §13.5 Table 30 GPIO/PWM_OUT row defines.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("The byte_msg_payload is presented at the interface"; GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=000b — this citation corrects the requirement text's own "Table 30", which is TC18's Table 30: Error codes in responses, not the evt-field table), TC18.txt L4093,L4116

requirements.title: PWM_OUT write semantics: Or/And/Xor/Add/Subtract combine against the previous state, per field
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmOutEndpoint::handle_write shall apply WriteSemantics::Or/::And/::Xor/::Add/::Subtract independently against `period` and `active_duration`, each within its own uint16_t range (Add/Subtract saturating at 0x0000/0xFFFF rather than wrapping, per §13.5 Table 30's saturation note and independently of GPIO's own 32-bit saturation bound for the same write semantics).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=001b-011b,101b-110b; "While doing additions and subtractions neither overflows nor wrap-arounds shall occur. The values are saturated at 0x0000 on the low side and 0xFFFF at the high side." — this citation corrects the requirement text's own "Table 30" and the prior "L3694-3714" line range, both of which pointed at unrelated sequencer-state-machine text), TC18.txt L4094-4119

requirements.title: PWM_OUT write semantics: Reserved and Reconfigure rejected
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmOutEndpoint::handle_write shall return an error without modifying its state for WriteSemantics::Reserved, and shall return rcp::endpoint::EndpointErrc::non_combinable_write_semantics for WriteSemantics::Reconfigure (PWM_OUT defines no Reconfigure target of its own).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 (GPIO/PWM_OUT row, evt[2:0]=100b "reserved – request shall be ignored and an err-response with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD shall be sent"; evt[2:0]=111b "used to change the configuration of the endpoint"), TC18.txt L4106-4116

requirements.title: PWM_IN response-only read model and PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmInEndpoint::handle_read shall return PwmErrc::no_signal before any record_measurement call and again after clear_signal(), and shall otherwise return the most recently recorded PwmValue.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.1 ("If the period of the incoming signal exceeds the configured maximum allowed period or if the external PWM source stops, the PWM_IN endpoint will detect this and if enabled within the EP_config (EP_RESP_ON_ERR) notify the RC Client with an error response message."; error code PWM_IN_NO_SIGNAL(9), Table 30: Error codes in responses), TC18.txt L5078-5080

requirements.title: PWM_IN rising/falling edge trigger signals (Table 44)
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmInEndpoint::record_measurement shall notify both the RisingEdge and FallingEdge trigger signals on every call (one full input-capture cycle spans both edges); record_edge shall notify exactly the one signal it is given, without the other, matching TC18 Table 44's two independent trigger outputs rather than an invented single combined signal.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.6.1 Table 47 ("pwmi trigger outputs"; 0 = rising edge of PWM_IN signal, 1 = falling edge of PWM_IN signal — this citation corrects the requirement's own "§13.7.5.1 Table 44", which is PWM_OUT's section and GPIO's functional-config table respectively, not PWM_IN's trigger table), TC18.txt L5078-5087

requirements.title: PwmErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::make_error_code(PwmErrc::no_signal) shall report rcp::pwm::pwm_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: PwmInEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before reading
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmInEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to handle_read() with out_value unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without touching out_value or any measured state.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; PWM_IN's own request-handling section explicitly defers to this same rule rather than redescribing it: §13.7.6.3 ("The interpretation of the evt-bits is described in the section 'The usage of evt bits in requests'"), TC18.txt L5168-5180; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: PwmInEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::pwm::PwmInEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported without touching out_value or any measured state and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary read or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported and ADC's AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: message_timestamp-repurposing request_type decode/encode (mtv=0)
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_request_type shall return RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed when mtv is true, shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the top byte of message_timestamp is not one of the 8 defined opcodes, and shall otherwise recover the opcode and the remaining 7 parameter bytes exactly as produced by encode_request_type for the same inputs; rcp::request::make_conditional_request shall always build an ACF_GBB AcfMessageInfo with mtv clear. The repurposed slot is the ACF_GBB message_timestamp slot at wire octets 4-11 (see REQ-WIRE-005), whose first octet carries the opcode.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("Different types of conditional requests"), TC18.txt L1260-1267

requirements.title: Request categories and execution-priority ordering
requirements.text: rcp::request::category_of shall map the 3 cancellation opcodes to RequestCategory::Cancellation, each of the 5 conditional opcodes to its own category, and std::nullopt to RequestCategory::Standard; rcp::request::select_next_due shall pick the candidate with the lowest priority_rank among due candidates and shall break ties within a category by lowest arrival_seq (FIFO), returning std::nullopt for an empty input.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3652-3660

requirements.title: Compound/compound-wait optional-feature bundling
requirements.text: rcp::request::validate_feature_bundles shall return RequestErrc::compound_bundle_incomplete whenever FeatureSet::compound or FeatureSet::compound_wait is set unless compound, compound_wait, clear_non_safestate, and sequencer_count >= kMinCompoundSequencers (4) are all simultaneously true, and shall accept every other combination of triggered/chained/timed/clear_single independently of compound support.
requirements.tc18: §12.2 ("Optional support of compound requests comes as bundle of - Support of compound requests (request types 0x0F and 0x8F) ... Implementation of at least four sequencers (see 12.10) - Clear all non-safestate requests from an EP request storage"), TC18.txt L2408-2413

requirements.title: Sequencer-state default value and finalization advance rule
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::ensure_size shall fill newly added slots with kDefaultState (1), never the storage's own zero-initialization default, shall never shrink existing storage, and try_advance shall increment a sequencer only when its current value equals the supplied expected_start, leaving it unchanged (and reporting out_advanced=false, not an error) otherwise; both accessors shall return RequestErrc::index_out_of_range for an out-of-bounds index.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 ("In RF state the state of sequencer cmp_sequencer is set to cmp_next_state if the sequencer state still equals the cmp_start_state, else the sequencer state is not changed."), TC18.txt L3702-3703

requirements.title: Cancellation kinds and shared cancellation semantics
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::cancel_single shall cancel a Pending/Started request and cascade cancellation to every transitive chained successor, and shall return RequestErrc::request_not_found for an unknown transaction or one that is UnderExecution/Finalized/already Canceled; cancel_all shall cancel every Pending/Started record (optionally skipping is_safety records when non_safestate_only is set) without disturbing any UnderExecution or Finalized record; a canceled request's outcome_of shall report RequestErrc::request_canceled.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("If a request is cancelled to which a request is chained, then the chained successors shall be cancelled by the RC Server as well."), TC18.txt L1978-1979

requirements.title: Request lifecycle state machine: pending -> started -> under_execution -> finalized
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger shall only permit the single-step forward sequence Pending->Started->UnderExecution->Finalized, returning RequestErrc::invalid_lifecycle_transition for any other requested transition and RequestErrc::unknown_transaction for an untracked id; submit shall return RequestErrc::transaction_num_collision for a transaction_num already tracked; finalize shall drive SequencerTable::try_advance for a Compound/CompoundWait record's sequencer_index/expected_start_state as its side effect.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 ("Once a request has been filed into an EP request storage, it is in the state \"request pending\". When the request is due for execution... it enters the state \"request started\" (RS)... The lifecycle advances to \"request under execution\" (RE)... and then to \"request finalized\" (RF)"), TC18.txt L3679-3682

requirements.title: Chained-successor propagation on predecessor finalization
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::finalize shall, for every record whose chained_predecessor equals the finalized transaction_num, cascade-cancel that successor iff rcp::request::should_execute_chained(successor.cs, errored) is false, and shall leave every such successor untouched when the predecessor finalized with errored=false.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 ("cs Conditional start 0b: request will be executed even in case the previous request returned an error 1b: request will not be executed in case the previous request returned an error... error response with error code = CHAIN_ABORTED. In case the chain is repetitive as per initial request it starts over."), TC18.txt L1833-1838

requirements.title: The cs field's dual meaning (compound-wait vs. chained)
requirements.text: rcp::request::compound_wait_check_of shall map cs=true to CompoundWaitCheck::Immediate and cs=false to CompoundWaitCheck::AfterChangeOnly; rcp::request::should_execute_chained shall return true whenever cs is true regardless of predecessor_errored, and shall return true iff predecessor_errored is false when cs is false.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 ("If cs = 0, then compound wait request is due for execution, when the sequencer is in the cmpw_start_state. If cs = 1, then compound wait request is due for execution, when EP output state has changed after the sequencer reached the cmpw_start_state."), TC18.txt L1514-1516

requirements.title: RequestErrc is a distinct error category with non-empty, distinct messages
requirements.text: Every rcp::request::RequestErrc value shall report rcp::request::request_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message distinct from every other RequestErrc value's message.

requirements.title: decode_request_type accepts exactly the three 0x8x safety-tagged opcodes
requirements.text: rcp::request::is_valid_request_type and decode_request_type shall accept RequestTypeOpcode::CompoundSafety (0x8F), CompoundWaitSafety (0x8B), and TriggeredSafety (0x8E) as valid opcodes, round-tripping their parameter bytes exactly as the eight pre-existing opcodes do, and shall reject every other MSB-set byte value as RequestErrc::unknown_request_type.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("0x0F, 0x8F Compound ... 0x0B, 0x8B Compound wait ... 0x0E, 0x8E Triggered"), TC18.txt L1260-1267

requirements.title: Safety-tagged opcodes share their base opcode's priority category
requirements.text: rcp::request::is_safety_variant shall return true for exactly CompoundSafety/CompoundWaitSafety/TriggeredSafety and false for every other RequestTypeOpcode; rcp::request::category_of shall map each safety-tagged opcode to the same RequestCategory as its corresponding base opcode (Compound, CompoundWait, Triggered).
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state"), TC18.txt L1258-1259

requirements.title: request_record_for derives RequestRecord::is_safety from the opcode
requirements.text: rcp::request::request_record_for shall set the returned RequestRecord's is_safety field to is_safety_variant(*type) when type has a value, to false when type is std::nullopt (the standard request kind), and the resulting record shall be excluded from cancellation by RequestLedger::cancel_all(non_safestate_only=true) if and only if is_safety is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 ("Clear all non-safestate requests from an EP request storage that have been received in the same stream as the request for cancellation. In this case the request type (first byte in the message_timestamp field) is 0x06."), TC18.txt L2056-2057

requirements.title: LIN's ep_type id is 0x06
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeLin shall equal 0x06.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"; row "0x06 LIN"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: LIN is a raw-byte-pusher with no frame-level concepts
requirements.text: rcp::lin::LinEndpoint::transfer shall record the exact byte sequences passed as out_bytes and in_bytes, retrievable via last_sent()/last_received(), performing no checksum selection, PID generation, schedule-table lookup, or any other LIN frame-structure interpretation of either sequence, including for an empty byte sequence.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.3 ("The Byte Msg Payload is the payload to be used on the Lin bus."; Figure 39 – "lin request format" shows only an opaque "Lin payload" region, with no PID/checksum/schedule sub-fields), TC18.txt L5719-5736

requirements.title: LIN TransferComplete and NoResponse trigger signals
requirements.text: rcp::lin::LinEndpoint::transfer shall notify only TransferComplete for a responded transfer (responded=true) and shall notify only NoResponse and return LinErrc::no_response for an unresponded transfer (responded=false).
requirements.tc18: §13.7.10.1 ("It sends the bytes provided by the RC Client in the byte_msg_payload on the bus as response to a pending read request. With pending read-requests the LIN endpoint checks each received message against the byte_msg_payload and if a match under the conditions given by evt[2:0] is found a reply is sent if op = 0."), TC18.txt L5691-5693

requirements.title: LinErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::lin::make_error_code(LinErrc::no_response) shall report rcp::lin::lin_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: LinEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before transferring
requirements.text: rcp::lin::LinEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to transfer() with out_bytes/in_bytes/responded unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without recording anything as sent or received.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: LinEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::lin::LinEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return LinErrc::config_write_not_supported without recording anything as sent or received and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary transfer or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported, ADC's AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported, and PWM_IN's PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. LinErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: CAN's ep_type id is 0x0B
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeCan shall equal 0x0B.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"; row "0x0B CAN"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: CAN identifier range validation
requirements.text: rcp::can::validate_identifier shall accept a CanIdentifier whose value is within its own width's range (0..0x7FF for extended=false, 0..0x1FFFFFFF for extended=true) and shall return CanErrc::identifier_out_of_range for a value exceeding that range.

requirements.title: CAN frame-format payload ceilings, data frames only
requirements.text: rcp::can::validate_frame shall accept a CanDataFrame whose data length is within its FrameFormat's own ceiling (kMaxClassicalPayload=8 for Classical, kMaxFdPayload=64 for Fd) and shall return CanErrc::payload_exceeds_format_limit when that ceiling is exceeded; this header shall define no remote-frame request or response shape.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("Sending remote frames is not supported."; note: the 8-byte Classical / 64-byte FD numeric payload ceilings are standard CAN/CAN-FD facts this implementation applies, not independently restated with those numbers in the TC18 extract itself), TC18.txt L5887

requirements.title: CAN XL accepted single-AVTPDU payload limitation
requirements.text: rcp::can::validate_frame shall accept a FrameFormat::Xl frame whose data length is within kMaxXlPayloadSingleAvtpdu, shall return CanErrc::xl_payload_exceeds_single_avtpdu_bound for a length between kMaxXlPayloadSingleAvtpdu (exclusive) and kMaxXlPayloadSpec (inclusive), and shall return CanErrc::payload_exceeds_format_limit for a length exceeding kMaxXlPayloadSpec (2054), consistent with ROADMAP.md milestone 52's already-decided fragmentation no-go.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.3 ("For CAN XL this can be up to 2054 bytes (2048 + 6, see below), which requires segmentation, which is supported by the fields 'ms' and 'segment_num'."), TC18.txt L5859-5860

requirements.title: CAN per-phase bit-timing register sets
requirements.text: rcp::can::CanEndpoint::configure_bit_timing shall store the arbitration, fd_data, and xl_data CanBitTimingPhase register sets independently of one another, retrievable unchanged via bit_timing().
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("can functional configuration"; "CAN bit time register 1"/"2"/"3" rows at 0x000C/0x0010/0x0014 defining bit times for Classical CAN/CAN FD/CAN XL respectively), TC18.txt L5795-5836

requirements.title: CAN-XL-specific acceptance/receive filters
requirements.text: rcp::can::CanEndpoint::receive shall accept every frame when its format-scoped filter bank is empty, shall drop a frame matching no entry in that bank when the bank is non-empty (per rcp::can::acceptance_filter_matches's masked-id comparison), and shall match a FrameFormat::Xl frame against xl_receive_filters rather than the general acceptance_filters bank whenever xl_receive_filters is non-empty.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.11.2 Table 56 ("can functional configuration"; "acceptance filter 1"-"4" rows, "acceptance filter for CAN XL", and "receive filter 1"-"4" rows, "ID filter for frame reception"; the extracted table's exact masked-id matching algorithm is this implementation's own, the register fields themselves are spec-sourced), TC18.txt L5801-5836

requirements.title: CAN has no trigger-signal table; CanErrc is a distinct error category
requirements.text: rcp::can::CanEndpoint shall expose no TriggerRegistry accessor or signal-id helper, unlike every other device-facing endpoint type in this codebase, and rcp::can::make_error_code(CanErrc::identifier_out_of_range) shall report rcp::can::can_category() as its category with a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: CanEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before transmitting
requirements.text: rcp::can::CanEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to transmit() with frame unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without recording anything as transmitted (last_transmitted() left untouched).
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: CanEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::can::CanEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return CanErrc::config_write_not_supported without recording anything as transmitted and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary transmit or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported, ADC's AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported, PWM_IN's PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported, and LIN's LinErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. CanErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: ISELED's ep_type id is 0x0C
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeIseled shall equal 0x0C.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"; row "0x0C ISELED"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: ISELED Instruction/Address/Data request and Address/Data response shape
requirements.text: rcp::iseled::IseledEndpoint::transact shall record the exact IseledRequest (instruction/address/data) and IseledResponse (address/data) fields passed to it, retrievable via last_request()/last_response(), for a request and response whose fields fit their documented wire widths.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.3 Figure 41 – "iseled request format" (Instruction | Address | Data1 | Data2 | Data3 | padding), TC18.txt L5981-5995; response shape per Figure 42 – "iseled response format" (Address | Data[11:0] | CRC (optional) | rsvd), TC18.txt L6006-6014

requirements.title: ISELED 12-bit address / 12-bit data field-width validation
requirements.text: rcp::iseled::validate_request shall return IseledErrc::field_out_of_range when instruction exceeds kIseledInstructionMask (4 bits) or address exceeds kIseledFieldMask (12 bits); rcp::iseled::validate_response shall return IseledErrc::field_out_of_range when address or data exceeds kIseledFieldMask (12 bits); rcp::iseled::IseledEndpoint::transact shall propagate either failure without recording the request/response or firing TransferComplete.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.3 ("A response always contains the 12 bit address and 12 bit data plus the optional 4 bit CRC."), TC18.txt L6004

requirements.title: ISELED TransferComplete and NativeCrcError trigger signals
requirements.text: rcp::iseled::IseledEndpoint::transact shall notify only TransferComplete for a transaction whose response native CRC verifies (or carries none), and shall notify only NativeCrcError and return IseledErrc::native_crc_mismatch for a transaction whose response native CRC does not verify.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.12.1 ("The optional CRC generation as specified in the ISLED standard can be enabled. If so, the CRC will be generated and attached to the write messages to the ISELED network. For read data accordingly the CRC will be also calculated and checked."), TC18.txt L5910-5912 (correcting this entry's citation, which the original batch pointed at TC18-13.7.12.1-002 — the adjacent trigger-event clause — instead of this CRC-check clause, which actually matches the requirement's own NativeCrcError/native_crc_mismatch subject; NOTE: this entry's title/text still describe a NativeCrcError signal and IseledErrc::native_crc_mismatch that rcp/iseled.hpp's issue #71/cpp-RCP-02 fix already removed — the current header and tests/test_iseled.cpp only exercise the single TransferComplete signal; flagging the stale title/text for the maintainers rather than editing content outside this metadata-only pass's scope)

requirements.title: IseledErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::iseled::make_error_code(IseledErrc::native_crc_mismatch) shall report rcp::iseled::iseled_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: IseledEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before transacting
requirements.text: rcp::iseled::IseledEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to transact(request, response) with both arguments unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without recording anything as the last request/response (last_request()/last_response() left untouched) and without firing TransferComplete.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: IseledEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
requirements.text: rcp::iseled::IseledEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return IseledErrc::config_write_not_supported without recording anything as the last request/response and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary transaction or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported, ADC's AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported, PWM_IN's PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported, LIN's LinErrc::config_write_not_supported, CAN's CanErrc::config_write_not_supported, and UART's UartErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. IseledErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: MDIO's ep_type id is 0x0D
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeMdio shall equal 0x0D.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"; row "0x0D MDIO"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: MDIO mdio_payload width validation per mdio_mode
requirements.text: rcp::mdio::payload_width_bits shall return 16 for MdioMode::MmdSingleWord, MdioMode::MmdMultiWord, and MdioMode::MmsSingleWord regardless of mms_is_0_or_1, and shall return 32 for MdioMode::MmsMultiWord only when mms_is_0_or_1 is true (16 otherwise); rcp::mdio::validate_request shall return MdioErrc::payload_exceeds_mode_width when mdio_payload exceeds that width and shall accept every payload at or below it.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.13.3 Table 60 ("Usage of ABB message for mdio requests"; "mdio_payload for MMD, data fields are 16 bits. for MMS0 & 1: data fields are 32 bits. For other MMS, data fields are 16 bits"), TC18.txt L6080-6088

requirements.title: MDIO register write-then-read round-trip
requirements.text: rcp::mdio::MdioEndpoint::transact shall, for a given (mdio_mode, mdio_address) key, return the value most recently written to that register on a subsequent read, and shall return 0 for a register that has never been written.

requirements.title: MDIO mdio_mode keeps each mode's register space distinct
requirements.text: rcp::mdio::MdioEndpoint::transact shall key a register access on (mdio_mode, mdio_address) such that it never observes a value written under a different mdio_mode at the same mdio_address, and shall notify TransferComplete on every request regardless of mdio_mode.

requirements.title: MdioErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::mdio::make_error_code(MdioErrc::phy_address_out_of_range) shall report rcp::mdio::mdio_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: MdioEndpoint::handle_request applies Table 33 Row 2 evt[2:0] classification before transacting
requirements.text: rcp::mdio::MdioEndpoint::handle_request shall classify its evt_op argument via rcp::endpoint::evt_row2_kind_of (masking to the low 3 bits first) and, for EvtRow2Kind::Plain, shall delegate to transact(request, out) with both arguments unchanged; for EvtRow2Kind::Reserved, shall return endpoint::EndpointErrc::reserved_evt_row2 without recording anything as the last request (last_request() left untouched, no register written or read) and without firing TransferComplete.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33 ("ADC, PWM_IN, I²C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO: 000b to 110b reserved – request to be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD" / "111b: The byte_msg_payload is not presented to the interface but used to change the configuration of the endpoint (see 12.7.1)"), TC18.txt L4085-4092; corroborating worked example resolving the evt=000b ambiguity in Table 33's own favor: §13.7.9.3 Figure 34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request", ADC endpoint, evt field all-zero), TC18.txt L5590-5607

requirements.title: MdioEndpoint::handle_request reports config-write (evt[2:0]==111b) as not yet supported
