requirements.text: rcp::mdio::MdioEndpoint::handle_request, for EvtRow2Kind::ConfigWrite (evt[2:0]==111b), shall return MdioErrc::config_write_not_supported without recording anything as the last request and without crashing, rather than silently accepting the request as an ordinary transaction or silently doing nothing; full §12.7.1 configuration-write handling is deliberately deferred to a follow-up milestone, the same scope decision I2C's I2cErrc::config_write_not_supported, ADC's AdcErrc::config_write_not_supported, PWM_IN's PwmErrc::config_write_not_supported, LIN's LinErrc::config_write_not_supported, CAN's CanErrc::config_write_not_supported, UART's UartErrc::config_write_not_supported, and ISELED's IseledErrc::config_write_not_supported already made. MdioErrc::config_write_not_supported shall report a non-empty diagnostic message in its own error_category.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.1 ("This can be done by setting evt[2:0] = 111b in request as described above."; Figure 19 – "Configuration request"; "The data of the byte_msg_payload from a write request is written into the section of the EP that is addressed by the byte_bus_id."), TC18.txt L2844-2865

requirements.title: Wakeup control's ep_type id is 0x01
requirements.text: rcp::endpoint::kEndpointTypeWakeup shall equal 0x01.
requirements.tc18: §13.2 Table 32 ("ep_type values"; row "0x01 WakeUp"), TC18.txt L3998-4017

requirements.title: SleepCMD is a fixed opcode, distinct from rcp::sequencer's RequestTypeOpcode taxonomy
requirements.text: rcp::wakeup::kSleepCmd shall equal 0xA5; rcp::wakeup::decode_sleep_cmd shall accept only that exact byte value and return WakeupErrc::not_sleep_cmd for every other byte (including 0x8x safety-tagged sequencer opcode bytes); rcp::wakeup::WakeupEndpoint::handle_sleep_cmd shall transition to asleep on kSleepCmd and shall leave state unchanged and return an error for any other byte.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.3 ("SleepCMD is coded as 0xA5."), TC18.txt L4565

requirements.title: Wake-source pin monitoring
requirements.text: rcp::wakeup::WakeupEndpoint::record_wake_source_event shall set the corresponding bit in wake_source_pins() and shall clear is_asleep(), and clear_wake_source_pins() shall reset the accumulated mask to 0 without affecting is_asleep() or the handshake-pending state.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.2 Table 39 ("wup_status...Indication of wake-up source, writing '1' clears the flag. Each bit represents a wake-up source"), TC18.txt L4503-4506

requirements.title: Repeating WakeUp message handshake for hot-start-from-Sleep
requirements.text: rcp::wakeup::WakeupEndpoint::record_wake_source_event shall arm wakeup_message_pending() until acknowledge_wakeup() is called, wakeup_message_pending() shall continue reporting true across repeated calls while armed, and handle_sleep_cmd(kSleepCmd) shall clear any handshake left pending from a prior wake cycle.
requirements.tc18: §13.7.2.1 ("After establishing a network connection, the WakeUp endpoint sends repetitive messages. The timing interval is configurable (flush_time)."), TC18.txt L4488-4489

requirements.title: WakeupErrc is a distinct error category with a non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::wakeup::make_error_code(WakeupErrc::not_sleep_cmd) shall report rcp::wakeup::wakeup_category() as its category and shall have a non-empty diagnostic message.

requirements.title: Loan releases exactly once, via destruction or ret()
requirements.text: rcp::Loan shall invoke its bound release function exactly once over its lifetime, whether that release happens via destruction or an explicit ret() call, and a default-constructed Loan (no release function bound) shall be safe to destroy.

requirements.title: Annex J encapsulation sequence number round-trips and increments monotonically
requirements.text: rcp::udp::encode_annexj_datagram/decode_annexj_datagram shall round-trip a 4-byte big-endian encapsulation sequence number and the AVTPDU bytes that follow it unchanged, and rcp::udp::Client/rcp::udp::Server shall each maintain their own per-connection monotonically-incrementing counter for outgoing datagrams, exposed via Client::last_sent_encap_seq/last_recv_encap_seq and Server::last_recv_encap_seq(client).

requirements.title: Server/Client default to the Annex J control port (17221) when no port is given
requirements.text: rcp::udp::kAnnexJControlPort shall equal 17221, and rcp::udp::Server/rcp::udp::Client's port constructor parameter shall default to it so a caller that omits an explicit port binds/connects to 17221, while the explicit-port constructor form remains available.

requirements.title: EthHeader encode/decode round-trips dst/src MAC and EtherType
requirements.text: rcp::l2::encode_eth_header/decode_eth_header shall round-trip a 14-byte Ethernet header (destination MAC, source MAC, EtherType) unchanged, with the EtherType field always encoded as rcp::l2::kEtherType (0x22F0).

requirements.title: decode_eth_header rejects a buffer shorter than 14 bytes
requirements.text: rcp::l2::decode_eth_header shall return a non-zero std::error_code when given fewer than rcp::l2::kEthHeaderLen (14) bytes.

requirements.title: encode_l2_frame/decode_l2_frame round-trip an AVTPDU under the Ethernet header
requirements.text: rcp::l2::encode_l2_frame/decode_l2_frame shall round-trip a destination MAC, source MAC, EtherType, and the AVTPDU (NTSCF/TSCF header plus ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB message) it carries unchanged, for both NTSCF and TSCF framing.

requirements.title: Frame round-trips a TSCF-framed request with avtp_timestamp under L2 framing
requirements.text: rcp::l2::encode_frame/decode_frame shall round-trip a Frame carrying a TSCF header, including its timestamp_valid flag and 32-bit avtp_timestamp, unchanged, the same as rcp::udp::Frame's equivalent guarantee.

requirements.title: decode_l2_frame rejects a frame whose EtherType is not 0x22F0
requirements.text: rcp::l2::decode_l2_frame/decode_l2_multi_frame shall return rcp::l2::L2Errc::bad_ethertype when the decoded Ethernet header's EtherType field is not rcp::l2::kEtherType (0x22F0).

requirements.title: decode_l2_frame rejects a buffer shorter than the Ethernet header
requirements.text: rcp::l2::decode_l2_frame shall return a non-zero std::error_code when given fewer bytes than rcp::l2::kEthHeaderLen (14) requires.

requirements.title: MultiFrame round-trips two ACF_ABB messages packed into one L2 frame
requirements.text: rcp::l2::encode_l2_multi_frame/decode_l2_multi_frame shall round-trip two or more ACF_ABB/ACF_GBB messages packed into a single Ethernet frame's AVTPDU, per extraction §12.9.1.1's multiple-requests-in-one-frame requirement, the same as rcp::udp::MultiFrame's equivalent guarantee.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("An RCP frame may include multiple ACF-types (requests)."), TC18.txt L3617

requirements.title: l2::Server/l2::Client round-trip a real Ethernet frame byte-for-byte over a real interface pair
requirements.text: rcp::l2::Server and rcp::l2::Client shall exchange a real AF_PACKET/SOCK_RAW Ethernet frame over a real Linux network interface pair and round-trip an ACF request/response payload byte-for-byte, verified by tests/l2_veth_roundtrip.cpp against a real veth pair in the dedicated l2-veth CI job (needs CAP_NET_RAW/root, not exercised by the privilege-free ctest suite).

requirements.title: Server::FrameHandler reaches mock::Server's Table 24 suppression, conditional/cancellation-opcode routing, and E2E dispatch
requirements.text: rcp::l2::Server::set_frame_handler()'s FrameHandler shall receive the raw, unparsed ACF payload of one whole inbound L2 frame together with that frame's own stream_id and sequence_num (decoded via rcp::l2::decode_l2_frame_header()/decode_avtp_frame_header()), so that a caller wiring it to rcp::mock::Server::dispatch_frame()/dispatch_frame_e2e() reaches TC18 Table 24 response/ack routing suppression, conditional/cancellation-opcode routing, and E2E/fragment-aware dispatch for every request carried over L2 -- none of which rcp::l2::Server::Handler's pre-existing single-message signature (no stream_id parameter, routes only through rcp::mock::Server::dispatch()) can reach.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 (response/ack routing suppression)

requirements.title: is_unicast_mac classifies a destination MAC as unicast or multicast/broadcast
requirements.text: rcp::l2::is_unicast_mac shall return true iff the given MAC address's I/G (individual/group) bit -- the least-significant bit of its first octet -- is 0, matching standard IEEE 802.3 addressing and mirroring c-RCP's rcp_l2_mac_is_unicast() (REQ-L2-011 in that project's own catalog) -- the primitive TC18 §12.3.1.1/.2/.3's unicast-destination-required write-authorization rule (rcp::lifecycle::WriterCtx::via_non_unicast_frame, REQ-LIFECYCLE-027) needs to classify a frame's destination MAC.
requirements.tc18: §12.3.1.1/.2/.3 (write request accepted only when its frame's destination MAC is unicast)

requirements.title: acf_category() returns a unique, non-empty message per AcfErrc value
requirements.text: rcp::acf::acf_category().message() shall return a unique, non-empty string for each defined AcfErrc value (bad_acf_msg_type, bad_acf_msg_length).

requirements.title: encode_acf_abb writes the correct acf_msg_type regardless of the caller-supplied header
requirements.text: rcp::acf::encode_acf_abb shall write kAcfMsgTypeAbb into the encoded frame's acf_msg_type field, independent of any acf_msg_type value the caller's AcfMessageInfo happens to carry on entry.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("acf_msg_type 0x0E (ABB message)"), TC18.txt L1152-1153; ACF_GBB acf_msg_type=0x0D, e.g. TC18.txt L1447

requirements.title: AcfMessageInfo::mtv is a genuine two-state wire bit with no third "uncertain" state
requirements.text: rcp::acf::AcfMessageInfo::mtv shall be represented as a bool (exactly the two wire-defined states, valid/not-valid) and rcp::acf::effective_timestamp shall gate ACF_GBB message_timestamp use strictly on mtv being set, never treating an untimed message as implicitly valid.
requirements.tc18: §11.3 Responses, Table 17 ("mtv 0b - message_timestamp not valid (for ACF_GBB if PTP not working and for ACF_ABB) / 1b - message_timestamp valid (for ACF_GBB if PTP working correctly)"), TC18.txt L2246-2247 -- the general, exhaustive two-value mtv definition; also §11.2.1 Figure 7/Table 4 ("mtv 0b"), TC18.txt L1208-1222, the fixed-context row the earlier citation-backfill pass (PR #172) had already found

requirements.title: peek_msg_type reads the acf_msg_type byte without a full header decode
requirements.text: rcp::acf::peek_msg_type shall report the ACF message's acf_msg_type byte from a buffer as short as 1 byte, and shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer for a zero-length buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 (acf_msg_type is byte 0 of byte_message_info), TC18.txt L1142-1153

requirements.title: Encoded ACF_ABB message length matches header length plus payload
requirements.text: rcp::acf::encode_acf_abb shall produce a frame of exactly kAcfCommonHeaderLen + payload.size() bytes.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 (ABB byte_message_info, no timestamp), TC18.txt L1142-1149; ACF_GBB's additional 8-byte message_timestamp, e.g. TC18.txt L1447-1451

requirements.title: kAcfMsgTypeAbb/kAcfMsgTypeGbb carry the specification's own numeric values
requirements.text: rcp::acf::kAcfMsgTypeAbb shall equal 0x0E and rcp::acf::kAcfMsgTypeGbb shall equal 0x0D, the acf_msg_type values TC18 assigns to the ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB message formats respectively.

requirements.title: AcfMessageInfo::op is a genuine two-state wire bit matching the specification's single op bit
requirements.text: rcp::acf::AcfMessageInfo::op shall be represented as a bool (false = read, true = write), matching TC18's single-bit op field exactly rather than modeling a third encode-only state that could never appear on the wire.

requirements.title: request_header_constraints_valid validates a request's fixed-value fields
requirements.text: rcp::acf::request_header_constraints_valid(hdr, cs_has_meaning) shall return true iff hdr's hs, rsp, and err fields are all false, and cs is false unless cs_has_meaning is true (the compound-wait/chained exemption).

requirements.title: evt_row2_is_plain implements Table 33's shared ADC/PWM_IN/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO rule
requirements.text: rcp::acf::evt_row2_is_plain(evt) shall return true iff (evt & 0x7) == 0, per TC18 Table 33's rule for the {ADC, PWM_IN, I2C, LIN, CAN, UART, ISELED, MDIO} endpoint-type row.
requirements.tc18: §13.5 Table 33, TC18.txt L3666-3710 (the reserved-range wording); §13.7.9.3 Figure 33/34 ("RC Client sends a standard read request" / ADC response with 8 measurements), the corroborating worked example resolving the ambiguity in Table 33's own favor for evt=000b

requirements.title: compound_wait_evt_valid rejects exactly the reserved 011b value
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_evt_valid(evt) shall return true iff (evt & 0x7) != 0x3, per TC18 §13.5.1: a compound-wait request's evt[2:0] selects one of eight comparison modes, of which 011b is reserved.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match applies the shared status-length rule before any mode-specific comparison
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall return false, regardless of comparison mode or buffer contents, when status_len < payload_len; otherwise it shall compare against only status's own first payload_len bytes.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1, TC18.txt L3735-3741 (length-capping rule and its own SPI example)

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=000b: exact match
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 000b, return true iff payload[0..payload_len) matches the length-capped current status exactly, byte for byte.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=001b: AND-with-1s-mask
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 001b, return true iff every bit position set to 1 in payload is also set to 1 in the length-capped current status.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=010b: AND-with-0s-mask
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 010b, return true iff every bit position set to 1 in payload is set to 0 in the length-capped current status.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=100b: leading-quadlet high-word >=
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 100b, return true iff the first two bytes of payload's own leading quadlet, read big-endian, are >= the same two bytes of status; it shall return false, never reading out of bounds, when payload_len < 4.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=110b: leading-quadlet low-word >=
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 110b, return true iff the last two bytes of payload's own leading quadlet, read big-endian, are >= the same two bytes of status; it shall return false, never reading out of bounds, when payload_len < 4.

requirements.title: build_error_response builds a TC18 §12.9.6 error response
requirements.text: rcp::acf::build_error_response shall build an ACF_ABB message carrying the given byte_bus_id and transaction_num, err = true, rsp = true, evt != kEvtAcknowledge, and a one-octet byte_msg_payload equal to the given WireErrorCode's numeric value.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.6 ("The error response shall contain the byte_bus_id and transaction number of the request. The error response shall contain a byte_msg_payload with an error code."), TC18.txt L3808-3809; §11.3.4, TC18.txt L2299-2301

requirements.title: peek_gbb_request_type peeks a GBB frame's own request_type without a full kind-specific decode
requirements.text: rcp::acf::peek_gbb_request_type shall return the octet at frame offset kAcfCommonHeaderLen (the message_timestamp region's own repurposed leading octet, shared identically by every conditional-request kind) as out_request_type and return true, iff frame_len >= 9 and the frame's own header reports acf_msg_type == kAcfMsgTypeGbb; it shall return false, leaving out_request_type unchanged, for an ACF_ABB frame or a too-short buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 (request_type/message_timestamp-repurposing scheme, common to every conditional request kind), TC18.txt L1299-1541

requirements.title: build_acknowledge_rejected_response builds TC18 §11.3.1's Acknowledge-shaped storage-admission-rejection response
requirements.text: rcp::acf::build_acknowledge_rejected_response shall build a response with evt[3:0] == kEvtAcknowledge, err = true, rsp = true, and a one-octet byte_msg_payload equal to the given WireErrorCode's numeric value -- classifying via response_kind_of() as Acknowledge, not ErrorResponse, distinct from build_error_response()'s §11.3.4 Error Response shape even though both carry err=1.
requirements.tc18: §11.3.1 Acknowledge (err=1 rejection sub-case, distinct from §11.3.4 Error Response), TC18.txt

requirements.title: encode_acf_gbb writes the correct acf_msg_type regardless of the caller-supplied header
requirements.text: rcp::acf::encode_acf_gbb shall write kAcfMsgTypeGbb into the encoded frame's acf_msg_type field, independent of any acf_msg_type value the caller's AcfMessageInfo happens to carry on entry.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("acf_msg_type 0x0E (ABB message)"), TC18.txt L1152-1153; ACF_GBB acf_msg_type=0x0D, e.g. TC18.txt L1447

requirements.title: Encoded ACF_GBB message length matches header length plus payload
requirements.text: rcp::acf::encode_acf_gbb shall produce a frame of exactly kAcfGbbMessageInfoLen + payload.size() bytes, with kAcfGbbMessageInfoLen equal to kAcfCommonHeaderLen plus the 8-byte message_timestamp field.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 (ABB byte_message_info, no timestamp), TC18.txt L1142-1149; ACF_GBB's additional 8-byte message_timestamp, e.g. TC18.txt L1447-1451

requirements.title: pad_len computes the zero-pad octet count to the next quadlet boundary
requirements.text: rcp::acf::pad_len(unpadded_len) shall compute the zero-pad octet count (0-3) needed to bring unpadded_len octets up to a whole number of quadlets.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Figure 7 / Table 4 ("ABB message standard request" / "Usage of ABB message for standard requests"), TC18.txt L1142-1170

requirements.title: kAcfMsgTypeGbb carries the specification's own numeric value
requirements.text: rcp::acf::kAcfMsgTypeGbb shall equal 0x0D, the acf_msg_type value TC18 assigns to the ACF_GBB message format (see REQ-ACF-017 for the ACF_ABB / 0x0E counterpart, tested by the same TEST_CASE).

requirements.title: decode_acf_message_info decodes op as a genuine two-state field
requirements.text: rcp::acf::decode_acf_message_info shall decode the wire op bit into AcfMessageInfo::op as a bool -- by construction, decode can never produce a third encode-only state distinct from read/write.

requirements.title: header_is_request identifies a decoded message as a request, not a response
requirements.text: rcp::acf::header_is_request(hdr) shall return true iff hdr's rsp bit is false; a received message whose rsp bit is set shall not be admitted as a request, per TC18's rsp=1b response marker.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match returns false for the reserved evt[2:0]=0x3 mode as its own defensive fallback
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall also return false for evt[2:0] = 0x3 (reserved), as its own defined fallback behaviour for a caller that does not gate on compound_wait_evt_valid() first.
requirements.tc18: §13.5.1, TC18.txt L3735-3741 (length-capping rule and its own SPI example)

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=101b: leading-quadlet high-word <=
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 101b, return true iff the first two bytes of payload's own leading quadlet, read big-endian, are <= the same two bytes of status; it shall return false, never reading out of bounds, when payload_len < 4.

requirements.title: compound_wait_match evt[2:0]=111b: leading-quadlet low-word <=
requirements.text: rcp::acf::compound_wait_match shall, for evt[2:0] = 111b, return true iff the last two bytes of payload's own leading quadlet, read big-endian, are <= the same two bytes of status; it shall return false, never reading out of bounds, when payload_len < 4.

requirements.title: peek_subtype reads the subtype byte from a buffer as short as 1 byte, and rejects an empty buffer
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::peek_subtype shall report the AVTPDU's subtype byte from a buffer as short as 1 byte, and shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer for a zero-length buffer.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 (subtype is byte 0 of both NTSCF Figure 6 and TSCF Figure 5), TC18.txt L1118-1138

requirements.title: TSCF-without-time-sync is dropped under the default (DROP) policy
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::should_drop_tscf shall return true iff subtype is kSubtypeTscf, server_time_sync_supported is false, and unsupported_time_sync_policy is TscfFallback::Drop -- this codec's own original, default disposition.
requirements.tc18: §11.1 ("In case time-synchronization is not supported, AVTPDUs having a TSCF header are dropped, and no response send."), TC18.txt L1140

requirements.title: avtp_category() returns a unique, non-empty message per AvtpErrc value
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::avtp_category().message() shall return a unique, non-empty string for each defined AvtpErrc value (short_buffer, bad_subtype, length_mismatch).

requirements.title: should_drop_tscf does not drop a TSCF-without-time-sync frame when policy is IGNORE
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::should_drop_tscf shall return false for a TSCF frame with server_time_sync_supported == false when unsupported_time_sync_policy is TscfFallback::Ignore, per TC18 §13.3's configurable alternative to §11.1's unconditional drop wording.
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("Requests may come within an AVTPDU with a presentation time (i.e. TSCF header). In case the RC Server does not support time synchronization, the presentation time shall be ignored, and the request(s) executed as if no presentation time were included or dropped depending on the configuration of the RC Server."), TC18.txt L4035-4038

requirements.title: decode_tscf_header populates the TSCF header's reserved0/reserved1 fields from the wire
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::decode_tscf_header shall decode bytes 16-19 into TscfHeader::reserved0 and bytes 22-23 into TscfHeader::reserved1 exactly as received, so a caller can evaluate TC18 §13.3's reserved-bytes-all-zero rule (see tscf_reserved_all_zero(), REQ-AVTP-031) against the real wire content rather than an assumed-zero default.
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("If the reserved bytes in the header are all zero, then the request shall be queued as if the header was in NTSCF format or dropped, depending on configuration."), TC18.txt L4039-4040

requirements.title: decode_tscf_header faithfully decodes tu regardless of its value (§13.3)
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::decode_tscf_header shall decode the wire tu (timestamp-uncertain) bit into TscfHeader::tu unchanged for both tu=0 and tu=1, without itself branching on its value -- TC18 §13.3's 'execute as if tu=0' rule is a caller-level policy, not a decode-time transformation.
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("In case the time stamp is uncertain (i.e. tu = 1), then this shall be executed as if tu = 0."), TC18.txt L4040-4041

requirements.title: tscf_reserved_all_zero returns true iff both reserved fields are zero (§13.3)
requirements.text: rcp::avtp::tscf_reserved_all_zero(hdr) shall return true iff hdr.reserved0 and hdr.reserved1 are both zero, the predicate TC18 §13.3's own reserved-bytes rule is built on.
requirements.tc18: §13.3 ("If the reserved bytes in the header are all zero, then the request shall be queued as if the header was in NTSCF format or dropped, depending on configuration."), TC18.txt L4039-4040

requirements.title: WireErrorCode assigns the governing spec's own numbered wire error codes
requirements.text: rcp::acf::WireErrorCode shall assign each enumerator the exact numeric value TC18 Table 27/Table 30 defines for it (UnsupportedCmd=1 .. ChainError=17), so encode_error_payload()'s single-octet byte_msg_payload matches the wire value a peer expects.

requirements.title: fragment_category() gives every FragmentErrc value a distinct, non-empty message
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::fragment_category().message() shall return a non-empty string for every rcp::fragment::FragmentErrc value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined error code mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: plan_count() always plans a payload that already fits in one fragment (including an empty payload) to exactly one segment
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::plan_count() shall return 1 for payload_len == 0 regardless of max_fragment_payload, and shall return 1 whenever payload_len <= max_fragment_payload.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.9 ("In case an AVTPDU containing a single ACF_type would exceed the 'Max_AVTPDUsize' fragmentation as supported in ACF_ABB and ACF_GBB by the ms-bit will be performed."), TC18.txt L3408-3409

requirements.title: plan_count() returns 0 when fragmentation is disabled or the split exceeds the representable segment count
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::plan_count() shall return 0 when max_fragment_payload == 0 and payload_len exceeds it, and shall return 0 when the resulting split would need more than kMaxIntermediateSegments intermediate segments to represent.

requirements.title: plan() plans a single ms=false segment for a payload that fits in one fragment
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::plan() shall, when plan_count() reports 1, write exactly one Segment spanning the whole payload with ms == false.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("ms 0b – the fragment sequence is completed with this ABB message"), TC18.txt L1233; §12.7.9 (Max_AVTPDUsize fragmentation trigger), TC18.txt L3408-3409

requirements.title: plan() contiguously covers a multi-segment payload with correctly numbered intermediate segments
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::plan() shall, when plan_count() reports more than 1, produce segments whose [offset, offset+len) ranges contiguously cover the whole payload, with every segment but the last carrying ms == true and a segment_num equal to its zero-based index, and the last segment carrying ms == false.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("ms 0b – the fragment sequence is completed with this ABB message / 1b - more data to follow in one or more subsequent ABB messages"; "read_size/segment_num if op = 0 this is read_size, else segment_num"), TC18.txt L1233-1235

requirements.title: plan() returns a distinct error code for each of its own precondition failures
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::plan() shall return ErrDisabled or ErrTooManySegments under the same conditions plan_count() returns 0 for, and shall return ErrBadSegmentCount when segment_count does not match plan_count()'s answer for the same payload_len/max_fragment_payload.

requirements.title: to_string(ReasmResult) never returns null and gives every result value a distinct message
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::to_string() shall return a non-null string for every rcp::fragment::ReasmResult value, including unrecognized ones, with each defined value mapped to a distinct message.

requirements.title: A freshly-constructed Reassembler starts empty and not collecting
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler's constructor shall leave the reassembler not collecting, with size() == 0 and data() == nullptr, and max_total_len set to the caller-supplied value.

requirements.title: Reassembler::reset() discards in-progress state while preserving max_total_len
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::reset() shall discard any in-progress reassembly and any previously reassembled payload, leaving the reassembler in the same state a freshly-constructed Reassembler with the same max_total_len would be in.

requirements.title: A Reassembler's destruction releases its internal storage without leaking
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler shall release its internal storage when destroyed without leaking, whether or not a fragment sequence was in progress at the time -- satisfied here by RAII over its own fixed-capacity std::array member (this class holds no heap-allocated buffer of its own to explicitly free; see fragment.hpp's own "Fixed-capacity from day one" comment), unlike c-RCP's rcp_fragment_reassembler_destroy(), which frees a realloc()-grown heap buffer.

requirements.title: Reassembler::feed() completes immediately for a never-fragmented (ms=false) first fragment
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::feed() shall, when fed a single ms=false fragment on a freshly-constructed-or-reset Reassembler, return ReasmResult::kComplete with that fragment's payload as the reassembled result, without entering the collecting state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("ms 0b – the fragment sequence is completed with this ABB message"), TC18.txt L1233

requirements.title: Reassembler::feed() requires the first ms=true fragment of a sequence to carry segment_num 0
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::feed() shall return ReasmResult::kErrOutOfOrder, without appending the fragment, when the first ms=true fragment fed to a freshly-constructed-or-reset Reassembler carries a segment_num other than 0.

requirements.title: Reassembler::feed() requires each subsequent ms=true fragment's segment_num to be exactly one more than the previous
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::feed() shall return ReasmResult::kErrOutOfOrder, without appending the fragment and without disturbing already-collected state, when an ms=true fragment's segment_num is not exactly one more than the previously accepted fragment's segment_num.

requirements.title: Reassembler::feed() completes a sequence on any ms=false fragment regardless of its own segment_num field value
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::feed() shall return ReasmResult::kComplete and append the fragment's payload when fed an ms=false fragment while collecting, without validating or consulting that fragment's segment_num argument.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("ms 0b – the fragment sequence is completed with this ABB message"), TC18.txt L1233

requirements.title: Reassembler::feed() rejects a fragment that would exceed max_total_len without mutating state
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::feed() shall return ReasmResult::kErrTooLarge, leaving the reassembler's already-collected state unchanged, when appending the fed fragment's payload would cause the reassembled total to exceed max_total_len (further capped, always, by this Reassembler's own fixed kDefaultReassemblyCapacity).
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_stream_max_request_size ... Max size of a request in bytes (longer requests will be rejected)"), TC18.txt L3230-3232

requirements.title: Reassembler::is_collecting() reports whether a fragment sequence is currently in progress
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::is_collecting() shall return true iff the reassembler has accepted at least one ms=true fragment since the last completed reassembly or reset, and false otherwise, without mutating the reassembler.

requirements.title: Reassembler::data()/size() return the reassembled payload and its length after a completed reassembly
requirements.text: rcp::fragment::Reassembler::data()/size(), called immediately after feed() has returned ReasmResult::kComplete, shall report a payload pointer and length equal to the concatenation, in segment_num order, of every fragment's payload accepted for that sequence.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.1 Table 4 ("ms"/"read_size/segment_num" fields – the mechanism by which a split message's fragments are numbered so they can be reassembled), TC18.txt L1233-1235

requirements.title: BufferPool destruction frees every buffer still in the free list
requirements.text: rcp::loan::BufferPool's destructor shall free every buffer currently in the pool's free list, then release the pool itself, without leaking.

requirements.title: new_buffer_pool() allocates an empty, open pool
requirements.text: rcp::loan::new_buffer_pool() shall return a non-null, open (ok()==true) rcp::loan::BufferPool with an empty free list (pooled_count() == 0).

requirements.title: per-response/acknowledge-stream transmit queue enforces an octet-budgeted capacity
requirements.text: rcp::respqueue::RespQueue shall provide an octet-budgeted FIFO of framed response/acknowledge messages (push()/push_seq()/pop()), with capacity enforced against a caller-supplied capacity_octets (regmap.hpp's ResponseQueueConfig::queue_size, quadlets already converted to octets by the caller), refusing a push that would exceed capacity_octets outright and leaving the queue unchanged when frame_len exceeds the entire configured capacity, unfixable by any amount of eviction. capacity_octets == 0 means unbounded.

requirements.title: Max_AVTPDUsize bounds every transmitted AVTPDU and is MTU-consistency-checkable
requirements.text: rcp::respqueue::RespQueue::push()/push_seq() shall refuse (queue unchanged) any single frame whose own length exceeds the caller-supplied max_avtpdu_size_octets (regmap.hpp's ResponseQueueConfig::max_avtpdu_size, quadlets already converted to octets); RespQueue::max_avtpdu_size_within_mtu() shall report whether a candidate max_avtpdu_size_octets value fits within a caller-supplied mtu_budget_octets, for use before ever constructing a RespQueue.

requirements.title: A single ACF message exceeding Max_AVTPDUsize is fragmented via the ms bit
requirements.text: rcp::respqueue::RespQueue::max_fragment_payload() shall derive, from max_avtpdu_size_octets and a caller-supplied ACF header length, the max_fragment_payload budget rcp/fragment.hpp's plan_count()/plan() need to split a payload too large for one AVTPDU, conservatively reserving the fixed ACF header plus the worst-case 3 octets of trailing pad so the resulting budget is always safe.

requirements.title: flush_on_count triggers transmission of the whole queue packed into Max_AVTPDUsize-bounded AVTPDUs
requirements.text: rcp::respqueue::RespQueue::should_flush() shall return true once the queue's own running octet total reaches or exceeds a caller-supplied flush_on_count_octets threshold; RespQueue::plan_batch() shall report how many of the queue's FIFO-ordered entries fit together within one max_avtpdu_size_octets-bounded AVTPDU, so a caller drains exactly that many via pop() and repeats until the queue is empty.

requirements.title: Flush_time forces transmission once the configured interval since the last transmission elapses
requirements.text: rcp::respqueue::RespQueue::should_flush_by_time() shall return false when flush_time_us == 0 ("flush only by count"), and otherwise return true once a caller-tracked elapsed_since_last_transmit_us reaches flush_time_us, independently of flush_on_count.

requirements.title: an empty response queue still emits a heartbeat AVTPDU on Flush_time expiry
requirements.text: PARTIAL: on Flush_time expiry the RC Server shall emit an AVTPDU from the queue even when that queue is empty, so the RC Client can observe that the server is alive. rcp::respqueue::RespQueue::should_flush_by_time() already fires identically for an empty queue, and RespQueue::plan_batch() already reports 0 for an empty queue -- so the empty heartbeat AVTPDU is fully constructible from existing primitives. What remains open: this is a protocol-primitives library, not a scheduler, and ships no emitter that actually drives this composition against a real clock and a real transport -- that composition is left to the integrator.

requirements.title: TC18 §12.9.4/§12.9.5: a completely-full response/acknowledge queue evicts the lowest-sequence_num entry and sets the overflow bit
requirements.text: rcp::respqueue::RespQueue::push()/push_seq() shall, once accepting an incoming frame would exceed capacity_octets or the queue's own fixed kMaxEntries slot bound, repeatedly evict the currently-queued entry with the numerically lowest sequence_num (not merely the FIFO-oldest) until enough capacity is freed, latching overflow() true on every eviction; a frame whose own length exceeds capacity_octets in its entirety shall be refused outright (queue unchanged, no eviction attempted).
requirements.tc18: §12.9.4/§12.9.5 (queue-full eviction and overflow-bit rule), see REQ-RMAP-059/061 for the byte-budget and per-message-ceiling siblings this rule is independent of

requirements.title: is_safety_variant() reports the MSB (0x80) of a RequestTypeOpcode
requirements.text: rcp::request::is_safety_variant() shall return true iff the opcode's 0x80 bit is set, i.e. iff type is exactly one of RequestTypeOpcode::CompoundSafety/CompoundWaitSafety/TriggeredSafety.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("If the MSB of the identifier (0x8x) is set the request is treated as a safety request and will not be deleted when the EP needs to go to safe state."), TC18.txt L1258-1259

requirements.title: is_compound() recognizes RequestTypeOpcode::Compound and its safety variant
requirements.text: rcp::request::is_compound() shall return true iff type == RequestTypeOpcode::Compound or type == RequestTypeOpcode::CompoundSafety.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 (request_type 0x0F/0x8F = Compound), TC18.txt L1262

requirements.title: is_compound_wait() recognizes RequestTypeOpcode::CompoundWait and its safety variant
requirements.text: rcp::request::is_compound_wait() shall return true iff type == RequestTypeOpcode::CompoundWait or type == RequestTypeOpcode::CompoundWaitSafety.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 (request_type 0x0B/0x8B = Compound wait), TC18.txt L1263

requirements.title: encode_compound_request() packs the step at the specification's own sub-field offsets
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_compound_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB-framed frame with mtv forced to false and shall write the repurposed message_timestamp region as: request_type at octet offset 0, step.start_state at offset 1, step.next_state at offset 2, step.sequencer_index at offset 3, step.exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and step.repeat_count as two big-endian octets at offsets 6-7, per encode_compound_step_params().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Figure 9 (compound-wait GBB sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1494-1506

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a frame shorter than the ACF_GBB header
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_compound_request() shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer (via acf::decode_acf_gbb() inside detail::decode_repurposed()) when the input is shorter than the ACF_GBB fixed header or its declared payload length.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a non-ACF_GBB message
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_compound_request() shall return AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type (via acf::decode_acf_gbb() inside detail::decode_repurposed()) when the leading octet does not identify an ACF_GBB message.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a message whose mtv is not untimed
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_compound_request() shall return RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed (via decode_request_type() inside detail::decode_repurposed()) when the decoded AcfMessageInfo::mtv is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() rejects a request_type it does not recognize
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_compound_request() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode is neither is_compound() nor is_compound_wait().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("first byte in message_timestamp field" -> "type of condition": 0x0F/0x8F Compound, 0x0B/0x8B Compound wait), TC18.txt L1254-1267

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() recovers every sub-field from the specification's own offsets
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_compound_request() shall, given a frame whose repurposed message_timestamp region carries the layout REQ-CMP-010 defines, return no error and recover type, byte_bus_id, transaction_num, evt_op, and every CompoundStep sub-field (start_state, next_state, sequencer_index, exec_delay, repeat_count) from those same offsets and widths via decode_compound_step_params().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 Figure 9 (compound-wait GBB sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1494-1506

requirements.title: encode_clear_non_safestate() encodes a fixed-length, opcode-0x06, mtv-untimed frame
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_clear_non_safestate() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame addressed to byte_bus_id, echoing transaction_num, with mtv forced to false and the message_timestamp region's leading byte equal to RequestTypeOpcode::ClearNonSafestate and its remaining 7 bytes zero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 (clear-non-safestate, request_type 0x06), TC18.txt L2093-2124

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() round-trips a frame produced by its own encoder
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_non_safestate() shall, given a frame produced by encode_clear_non_safestate(), return no error and recover the original byte_bus_id and transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Figure 15 (clear-non-safestate GBB layout), TC18.txt L2073-2082

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects a request_type other than ClearNonSafestate
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode is not RequestTypeOpcode::ClearNonSafestate, given the same short-frame/bad-msg-type/not-repurposed failure modes as decode_compound_request().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 (clear-non-safestate, request_type 0x06), TC18.txt L2093-2124

requirements.title: SequencerTable::advance_guard() is true iff the target sequencer is still in start_state
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::advance_guard() shall return true iff step.sequencer_index is a valid index into the table and the table's current state at that index is nonzero (enabled) and equal to step.start_state, and shall return false for an invalid index. It shall not treat a start_state of zero specially — that sentinel governs whether a request may start (REQ-CMP-025), not whether its sequencer is advanced afterwards.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 ("the state (cmp_next_state) the sequencer shall enter after the compound request has been executed (if the sequencer is still in cmp_start_state)"), TC18.txt L1385-1387

requirements.title: SequencerTable::exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= step.exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time, not in milliseconds.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 ("cmp_exec_delay: delay time between the sequencer reaching the state defined in start_state and the start of the execution of the request... execution shall happen even in case the state changes before the delay expired"), TC18.txt L1439-1442

requirements.title: SequencerTable::tick() advances the sequencer only once both the delay has elapsed and the guard holds
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::tick() shall set the target sequencer to step.next_state (via apply_next_state()) and return true iff both exec_delay_elapsed(step, elapsed) and advance_guard(step) hold; otherwise it shall leave the table unchanged and return false. When step.next_state is zero it shall leave the sequencer in its current state and still return true, per the "sequencer remains in the current state" sentinel apply_next_state() implements.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 / Figure 8 (GBB message for compound requests: request_type, cmp_start_state, cmp_next_state, cmp_sequencer, cmp_exec_delay, cmp_repetitions), TC18.txt L1379-1458; "If cmp_next_state is = 0 then the sequencer remains in the current state, when the execution is finalized.", TC18.txt L1387-1388

requirements.title: SequencerTable::tick() never advances a sequencer that has already left start_state, even after its delay elapses
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::tick() shall return false and leave the table unchanged when exec_delay_elapsed(step, elapsed) holds but the target sequencer's current state does not equal step.start_state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 Table 7 ("cmp_exec_delay: delay time between the sequencer reaching the state defined in start_state and the start of the execution of the request... execution shall happen even in case the state changes before the delay expired"), TC18.txt L1439-1442; §11.2.2.2 ("the state (cmp_next_state) the sequencer shall enter after the compound request has been executed (if the sequencer is still in cmp_start_state)"), TC18.txt L1385-1387

requirements.title: SequencerTable::wait_tick() advances the sequencer only once both condition_met and the guard hold
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::wait_tick() shall set the target sequencer to step.next_state (via apply_next_state()) and return true iff both condition_met and advance_guard(step) are true; otherwise it shall leave the table unchanged and return false. When step.next_state is zero it shall leave the sequencer in its current state and still return true, per the same sentinel REQ-CMP-021 names.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 ("When the check finds that the condition is met the cmpw_exec_delay needs to expire before a response is generated, else the request execution is finalized without further action."), TC18.txt L1480-1482; §11.2.2.2 ("the state (cmp_next_state) the sequencer shall enter after the compound request has been executed (if the sequencer is still in cmp_start_state)"), TC18.txt L1385-1387

requirements.title: SequencerTable::wait_tick() never advances a sequencer that has already left start_state, even on a condition match
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::wait_tick() shall return false and leave the table unchanged when condition_met is true but the target sequencer's current state does not equal step.start_state.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.3 ("When the check finds that the condition is met the cmpw_exec_delay needs to expire before a response is generated, else the request execution is finalized without further action."), TC18.txt L1480-1482

requirements.title: SequencerTable::start_condition_met() implements the "any state" start_state sentinel
requirements.text: rcp::request::SequencerTable::start_condition_met() shall return true iff step.sequencer_index is a valid index into the table, the table's current state at that index is nonzero (enabled), and either step.start_state is zero (the request starts in whatever enabled state the sequencer currently holds) or the current state equals step.start_state. It shall return false for an index the table does not hold and for a disabled (state==0) sequencer, including when start_state is zero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.2 ("If cmp_start_state = 0 then the request shall be started in any state unless the sequencer is disabled which will prohibit the execution of the compound request."), TC18.txt L1389-1391; same rule for compound-wait, §11.2.2.3, TC18.txt L1489-1491

requirements.title: encode_compound_request() packs evt_op into the shared ACF header, not one of step's repurposed sub-fields
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_compound_request() shall write its evt_op parameter into the encoded frame's AcfMessageInfo::evt_op field via acf::encode_acf_gbb(), independently of every CompoundStep sub-field packed into the repurposed message_timestamp region. For a compound-wait request this is the TC18 §13.5.1 comparison-mode selector; a plain compound request has no comparison of its own.

requirements.title: decode_compound_request() surfaces the decoded evt_op field
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_compound_request() shall, on success, populate out.evt_op with the decoded AcfMessageInfo::evt_op field, independently of every recovered CompoundStep sub-field.

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects a nonzero reserved message_timestamp octet
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RequestErrc::reserved_field_nonzero when any of message_timestamp's 7 trailing octets (every octet after the leading request_type byte) carries a set bit, since clear-non-safestate carries no sub-field of its own.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L2093-2097

requirements.title: decode_clear_non_safestate() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_non_safestate() shall return RequestErrc::evt_hs_cs_nonzero (via detail::check_evt_hs_cs_zero()) when the decoded AcfMessageInfo's evt_op, hs, or cs is nonzero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.2 Table 14 ("evt[2:0], hs, cs: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected with error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD"), TC18.txt L2118-2124

requirements.title: is_triggered() recognizes RequestTypeOpcode::Triggered and its safety variant
requirements.text: rcp::request::is_triggered() shall return true iff type == RequestTypeOpcode::Triggered or type == RequestTypeOpcode::TriggeredSafety.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 (request_type 0x0E/0x8E = Triggered), TC18.txt L1264; §11.2.2.5 ("Each endpoint may be configured to start a request upon receiving a selected trigger signal"), TC18.txt L1691

requirements.title: encode_triggered_request() packs the trigger-selection sub-fields at the specification's own offsets
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_triggered_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to false and shall write the repurposed message_timestamp region as: request_type at octet offset 0, step.trigger_source_ep at offset 1, step.trigger_signal_nr at offset 2, step.trigger_threshold at offset 3, step.exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and step.repeat_count as two big-endian octets at offsets 6-7, per encode_triggered_step_params().
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (trigger_source_ep/trigger_signal sub-field offsets), TC18.txt L1720-1721

requirements.title: decode_triggered_request() maps ACF decode failures to their RequestErrc equivalents
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_triggered_request() shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer or AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type (via detail::decode_repurposed()) when acf::decode_acf_gbb() reports the corresponding failure.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_triggered_request() rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_triggered_request() shall return RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed when the decoded mtv is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_triggered_request() rejects a non-triggered opcode and otherwise recovers every sub-field
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_triggered_request() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode does not satisfy is_triggered(), and shall otherwise populate out.type, out.byte_bus_id, out.transaction_num, a borrowed out.payload view, and every TriggeredStep sub-field from the offsets and widths REQ-TRIG-004 defines.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 Table 5 ("0x0E, 0x8E" -> "Triggered"), TC18.txt L1254-1267

requirements.title: triggered_enter_started() resets the trigger-occurrence counter
requirements.text: rcp::request::triggered_enter_started() shall set rt.occurrence_count to 0 and rt.started to true.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695

requirements.title: triggered_record_occurrence() counts only the trigger this request selected
requirements.text: rcp::request::triggered_record_occurrence() shall increment rt.occurrence_count and return true iff rt.started is true and the observed occurrence matches this request's own selection, i.e. source_ep == step.trigger_source_ep and signal_nr == step.trigger_signal_nr. It shall leave rt entirely unchanged and return false for an occurrence from any other endpoint or any other trigger signal number, and for any occurrence while rt.started is false.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695; §11.2.2.5 Table 10 ("trigger_source_ep defines the endpoint which issues the trigger... trigger_signal_nr defines the trigger number of the endpoint addressed by trigger_source_ep"), TC18.txt L1720-1721

requirements.title: triggered_threshold_reached() counts occurrences that must precede execution
requirements.text: rcp::request::triggered_threshold_reached() shall return true iff rt.occurrence_count > step.trigger_threshold, so that a trigger_threshold of zero is satisfied by one occurrence and a trigger_threshold of N by N+1 occurrences.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (trigger_threshold), TC18.txt L1722-1724

requirements.title: triggered_exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp::request::triggered_exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= step.exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time, not in milliseconds.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (trigger_exec_delay), TC18.txt L1725-1727

requirements.title: triggered_tick() only fires when started, the threshold is reached, the delay has elapsed, and the endpoint is idle
requirements.text: rcp::request::triggered_tick() shall return false and leave rt unchanged unless rt.started is true, triggered_threshold_reached(step, rt) holds, triggered_exec_delay_elapsed(step, elapsed) holds, and endpoint_idle is true.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695; "When the trigger_exec_delay timer has expired the state advances to RE as soon as the EP is idle and no request with higher priority is pending.", TC18.txt L3692-3693

requirements.title: triggered_tick() resets the runtime on a successful fire and advances no sequencer
requirements.text: When every condition REQ-TRIG-012 names holds, rcp::request::triggered_tick() shall reset rt.occurrence_count to 0 and rt.started to false and return true. It shall not read or write any SequencerTable state: a triggered request carries no sequencer, start_state, or next_state sub-field.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.3 Table 29 (Triggered request row: "Upon entering RS state the counted number of received trigger signals is reset to zero and newly arriving trigger signals are counted from zero. The execution delay timer is started."), TC18.txt L3690-3695; TC18.txt L3692-3693 (trigger_exec_delay expiry + EP-idle gating)

requirements.title: encode_chained_member() leaves every reserved sub-field octet zero
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_chained_member() shall write octets 1-3 and 6-7 of the repurposed message_timestamp region as all-zero. It shall not encode any chain_length or chain_position sub-field: the specification defines neither, and a member's position in a chain is its position among the enclosing AVTPDU's requests.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 Table 11 (chained request reserved fields), TC18.txt L1827-1830

requirements.title: encode_chained_member() packs chain_exec_delay and cs at the specification's own positions
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_chained_member() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to false, the opcode byte RequestTypeOpcode::Chained at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, chain_exec_delay as two big-endian octets at offsets 4-5, and cs encoded into AcfMessageInfo's own cs bit.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 Table 11 (chain_exec_delay, cs semantics), TC18.txt L1828-1839

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() maps ACF decode failures to their RequestErrc equivalents
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_chained_member() shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer or AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type (via detail::decode_repurposed()) when acf::decode_acf_gbb() reports the corresponding failure.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_chained_member() shall return RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed when the decoded mtv is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() rejects a non-chained opcode and otherwise recovers chain_exec_delay and cs
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_chained_member() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode is not RequestTypeOpcode::Chained, and shall otherwise populate out.byte_bus_id, out.chain_exec_delay (from offsets 4-5), out.cs, out.transaction_num, and a borrowed out.payload view.

requirements.title: RequestLedger's chained-successor propagation reads cs off the member about to run, about its predecessor's outcome
requirements.text: rcp::request::should_execute_chained(cs, predecessor_errored) shall return true whenever cs is false (RCP_CHAINED_CS_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR, execute regardless), and shall return true iff predecessor_errored is false when cs is true (RCP_CHAINED_CS_ABORT_ON_ERROR). RequestLedger::finalize()'s propagate_chain_completion() shall consult should_execute_chained() with each direct successor's own cs, not the finalizing predecessor's, and cascade_cancel() that successor (and, transitively, every one of its own chained_successors regardless of their cs) whenever should_execute_chained() returns false. A predecessor that finalizes with errored=false never aborts any successor, independent of cs.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 Table 11 (cs conditional-start semantics), TC18.txt L1833-1839

requirements.title: chained_exec_delay_elapsed() compares elapsed against chain_exec_delay
requirements.text: rcp::request::chained_exec_delay_elapsed() shall return true iff elapsed >= chain_exec_delay, both expressed in multiples of the addressed endpoint's configured ep_delay_time and measured from the moment the member's predecessor finalized.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 ("chain_exec_delay: Execution delay in multiples of ep_delay_time... for the request execution after the previous request has been finalized."), TC18.txt L1828-1829

requirements.title: decode_chained_member() rejects a non-zero reserved sub-field octet
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_chained_member() shall return RequestErrc::reserved_field_nonzero when any of octets 1-3 or 6-7 of the repurposed message_timestamp region carries a set bit.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.6 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request will be rejected" / "...shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L1827, L1830

requirements.title: timed_feature_enabled() requires the conditional-requests option bit set
requirements.text: rcp::request::timed_feature_enabled() shall return true iff regmap::kOptConditionalRequests is set in options, and false otherwise. cpp-RCP's svr_implemented_options bitmask is coarser than c-RCP's four independent per-feature bits (compound-wait/trigger/chained/time-sync); kOptConditionalRequests is the one bit this codebase already uses to mean "some conditional-request kind, including Timed, is implemented".
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 ("requests can be sent under TSCF header, where an avtp_timestamp is included... A second option is to convey the presentation time in the message_timestamp field of an ACF_GBB."), TC18.txt L1867-1868; conformance bullets "Implementation of gPTP (IEEE802.1as)" / "Support of timed request", TC18.txt L2399-2400

requirements.title: encode_timed_request() packs a 48-bit presentation_time and holds the reserved octet at zero
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_timed_request() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to false, the opcode byte RequestTypeOpcode::Timed at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, an all-zero reserved octet at offset 1, and presentation_time as six big-endian octets spanning offsets 2-7. It shall return std::nullopt, never a truncated frame, when presentation_time exceeds kTimedPresentationTimeMax.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Figure 13 (48-bit presentation_time offset), TC18.txt L1871-1882

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_timed_request() shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer or AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type (via detail::decode_repurposed()) when acf::decode_acf_gbb() reports the corresponding failure, and RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed when the decoded mtv is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() rejects a non-timed opcode and otherwise recovers the 48-bit presentation_time
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_timed_request() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode is not RequestTypeOpcode::Timed, and shall otherwise populate out.byte_bus_id, out.transaction_num, a borrowed out.payload view, and out.presentation_time from the six octets at offsets 2-7 of the repurposed region, in [0, kTimedPresentationTimeMax].

requirements.title: timed_too_far() is wraparound-safe in the 48-bit presentation-time domain
requirements.text: rcp::request::timed_too_far() shall compute presentation_time - now modulo kTimedPresentationTimeModulus (via detail::timed_forward_delta()), shall return false whenever that difference exceeds half the modulus (i.e. presentation_time is at or before now, via detail::timed_in_the_past()), and shall otherwise return true iff the difference exceeds max_horizon.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 ("The RC Server may reject the request, when the presentation_time is too far in the future, which is implementation dependent (error code = PRESENTATION_TIME_TOO_FAR)."), TC18.txt L1953-1954

requirements.title: timed_admit() reports TimedAdmission::RejectGptpFail whenever gptp_locked is false
requirements.text: rcp::request::timed_admit() shall return TimedAdmission::RejectGptpFail whenever gptp_locked is false, regardless of presentation_time, now, or max_horizon, taking priority over the presentation-time-too-far check.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 ("In case the time synchronization hasn't been established, timed requests (either in the format shown here or under TSCF header) shall be rejected and an error response shall be sent (error code = GPTP_FAIL)."), TC18.txt L1955-1956

requirements.title: timed_admit() reports RejectPresentationTimeTooFar or Accept when gPTP is locked
requirements.text: rcp::request::timed_admit() shall return TimedAdmission::RejectPresentationTimeTooFar when gptp_locked is true and timed_too_far(presentation_time, now, max_horizon) holds, and TimedAdmission::Accept otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 ("The RC Server may reject the request, when the presentation_time is too far in the future"), TC18.txt L1953

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() rejects a non-zero reserved octet
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_timed_request() shall return RequestErrc::reserved_field_nonzero when the reserved octet at offset 1 of the repurposed message_timestamp region (params[0]) carries any set bit.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Table 12 (reserved bits must be 0), TC18.txt L1906

requirements.title: decode_timed_request() rejects a timed request with hs or cs set
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_timed_request() shall return RequestErrc::unsupported_cmd when the decoded AcfMessageInfo's hs or cs bit is set.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 Table 12 (hs and cs shall both be 0b), TC18.txt L1911-1912

requirements.title: timed_due() reports whether a presentation_time has arrived
requirements.text: rcp::request::timed_due() shall return true iff presentation_time is at or before now in the same wrapping 48-bit domain timed_too_far() uses, i.e. iff the request's execution condition is satisfied.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.2.7 ("In any case the presentation_time is the earliest point in time, when the request shall be executed."), TC18.txt L1952

requirements.title: A request carried under a TSCF header is postponed until its own presentation time
requirements.text: rcp::server::Endpoint::admit()/admit_with_ack() shall, whenever the caller reports tv true (an enclosing TSCF header's own avtp_timestamp), postpone execution of the admitted request -- of any kind, Standard, Cancellation, or a conditional kind with its own start condition -- until avtp::extend_timestamp(avtp_timestamp, gptp_reference_now)'s reconstructed 48-bit instant is reached; select_due()/is_due() shall AND this envelope-level presentation gate with (not substitute for) each kind's own existing execution condition, and shall fail closed -- never report the request due -- whenever gptp_locked is false, regardless of how far in the past the gate's own instant already is.

requirements.title: encode_clear_all() encodes a zero-payload clear-all request
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_clear_all() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to false, the opcode byte set to RequestTypeOpcode::ClearAll, and the remaining repurposed sub-field bytes zeroed.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Figure 14 + Table 13 (clear-all, request_type 0x05), TC18.txt L1983-2050

requirements.title: decode_clear_all() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_all() shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer or AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type (via detail::decode_repurposed()) when acf::decode_acf_gbb() reports the corresponding failure, and RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed when the decoded mtv is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Figure 14 / Table 13 (Usage of GBB message to cancel all requests, request_type=0x05), TC18.txt L1983-2050; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis and §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_clear_all() rejects an opcode byte that is not ClearAll
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_all() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode is not RequestTypeOpcode::ClearAll, and shall otherwise populate out.byte_bus_id and out.transaction_num.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 13 (clear-all, request_type 0x05), TC18.txt L2024-2025

requirements.title: encode_clear_single() packs clear_transaction_num at the specification's own offset
requirements.text: rcp::request::encode_clear_single() shall produce an ACF_GBB frame with mtv forced to false, the opcode byte RequestTypeOpcode::ClearSingle at octet offset 0 of the repurposed message_timestamp region, clear_transaction_num at octet offset 3, and octets 1-2 and 4-7 all-zero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Figure 16 (clear-single, clear_transaction_num offset), TC18.txt L2140-2158

requirements.title: decode_clear_single() maps ACF decode failures and rejects a non-repurposed message_timestamp
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_single() shall return AvtpErrc::short_buffer or AcfErrc::bad_acf_msg_type (via detail::decode_repurposed()) when acf::decode_acf_gbb() reports the corresponding failure, and RequestErrc::timestamp_not_repurposed when the decoded mtv is true.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Figure 16 / Table 15 (Usage of GBB message to cancel a single, specific request, request_type=0x07, clear_transaction_num), TC18.txt L2140-2210; general ACF_GBB frame-validation basis and §11.2.2 ("conditional requests are sent using ACF_GBB having mtv = 0 (time stamp not valid) and using the bytes of the message_timestamp field to convey the execution condition"), TC18.txt L1255-1258

requirements.title: decode_clear_single() recovers clear_transaction_num from the specification's own offset
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_single() shall return RequestErrc::unknown_request_type when the decoded opcode is not RequestTypeOpcode::ClearSingle, RequestErrc::reserved_field_nonzero when any of octets 1-2 or 4-7 of the repurposed region carries a set bit, and shall otherwise populate out.byte_bus_id, out.transaction_num, and out.clear_transaction_num from octet offset 3.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 Table 15 (clear-single, clear_transaction_num), TC18.txt L2185

requirements.title: RequestLedger treats exactly Pending/Started records as cancellable
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::cancel_single()/cascade_cancel() shall treat a record as cancellable iff its state is RequestState::Pending or RequestState::Started, and shall report RequestErrc::request_not_cancellable (never cancelling it) for a record whose state is UnderExecution, Finalized, or already Canceled.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1977-1978

requirements.title: RequestLedger::cancel_single() reports request_not_found when the target was never tracked
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::cancel_single() shall return RequestErrc::request_not_found whenever the given transaction_num is not tracked by this ledger at all, regardless of what state it would otherwise have been in.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("The request initiating the cancellation will create an error response with the error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, when the clear_transaction_num was not found."), TC18.txt L2212-2213

requirements.title: RequestLedger::cancel_single() reports request_not_cancellable for a found request outside the cancellable window
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::cancel_single() shall return RequestErrc::request_not_cancellable whenever the target transaction_num is tracked but its state is UnderExecution, Finalized, or already Canceled — distinct from request_not_found, which is reserved for a transaction_num never tracked at all.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1977-1978

requirements.title: RequestLedger::cancel_single() cancels a found, cancellable request
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::cancel_single() shall transition the target record to RequestState::Canceled and set its outcome to RequestErrc::request_canceled, and return no error, whenever the target transaction_num is tracked and its state is Pending or Started.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("A request can be cancelled while it is pending and after it has been started until it is under execution. Requests under execution will not be aborted."), TC18.txt L1977-1978; §11.2.3.3 ("The request initiating the cancellation will create an error response with the error code = REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, when the clear_transaction_num was not found."), TC18.txt L2212-2213

requirements.title: Cancelling a chained request cascades to every transitive chained successor
requirements.text: rcp::request::RequestLedger::cancel_single() shall, via cascade_cancel(), transition to RequestState::Canceled not only the target record but every record transitively reachable through its own chained_successors list, so that cancelling a chain's first member also cancels every not-yet-executing successor in that chain.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3 ("If a request is cancelled to which a request is chained, then the chained successors shall be cancelled by the RC Server as well."), TC18.txt L1978-1979

requirements.title: decode_clear_all() rejects a nonzero reserved message_timestamp octet
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_all() shall return RequestErrc::reserved_field_nonzero when any of message_timestamp's 7 trailing octets (every octet after the leading request_type byte) carries a set bit, since clear-all carries no sub-field of its own.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 13 ("reserved: All bits shall be written as 0, else the request shall be rejected"), TC18.txt L2025

requirements.title: decode_clear_all() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_all() shall return RequestErrc::evt_hs_cs_nonzero (via detail::check_evt_hs_cs_zero()) when the decoded AcfMessageInfo's evt_op, hs, or cs is nonzero.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.1 Table 13 (evt/hs/cs field descriptions), TC18.txt L2026-2030

requirements.title: decode_clear_single() rejects nonzero evt[2:0], hs, or cs
requirements.text: rcp::request::decode_clear_single() shall return RequestErrc::evt_hs_cs_nonzero (via detail::check_evt_hs_cs_zero()) when the decoded AcfMessageInfo's evt_op, hs, or cs is nonzero. Distinct from REQ-CANCEL-007's own RequestErrc::reserved_field_nonzero check, which validates message_timestamp's own reserved octets, a different wire region from the ACF header's evt/hs/cs bits.
requirements.tc18: §11.2.3.3 ("Evt, hs and cs shall be zero"), Table 15, TC18.txt L2140-2185

requirements.title: RequestCategory and priority_rank() encode the cancellation > triggered > timed > compound > compound-wait > chained > standard ordering
requirements.text: rcp::request::priority_rank() shall return a strictly lower numeric value (via the RequestCategory enum's own declaration order: Cancellation=0 .. Standard=6) for RequestCategory::Cancellation than ::Triggered, for ::Triggered than ::Timed, for ::Timed than ::Compound, for ::Compound than ::CompoundWait, for ::CompoundWait than ::Chained, and for ::Chained than ::Standard.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3652-3663

requirements.title: select_next_due() orders by priority rank first and FIFO arrival second
requirements.text: rcp::request::select_next_due() shall return the index of the DueCandidate with the lowest priority_rank(category) among `due`, and among candidates of equal rank shall pick the one with the lowest arrival_seq (FIFO tie-break); it shall return std::nullopt for an empty input.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.2 ("In case two or more requests are due for execution then the priorities are as follows: 1. cancellation 2. triggered 3. timed 4. compound 5. compound wait 6. chained 7. standard"), TC18.txt L3652-3663; §12.9.2 ("When two or more requests with the same priority are due then starting the execution shall happen in the order with which the requests arrived in the EP request storage."), TC18.txt L3663-3664

requirements.title: frame_timing_consistent() is trivially true for NTSCF frames and empty member lists
requirements.text: rcp::request::frame_timing_consistent() shall return true whenever is_tscf is false, and shall return true whenever member_is_timed is empty, regardless of member_is_timed's contents.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("As the AVTPDU has either a TSCF or NTSCF header a mixture of requests with and without presentation time in a single frame is not possible. A presentation time from a TSCF header will be applied to all ACFtypes within the frame."), TC18.txt L3622-3624

requirements.title: frame_timing_consistent() rejects a TSCF frame mixing timed and untimed members
requirements.text: For is_tscf == true and a non-empty member_is_timed, rcp::request::frame_timing_consistent() shall return true iff every entry in member_is_timed equals member_is_timed[0], and false otherwise.
requirements.tc18: §12.9.1.1 ("As the AVTPDU has either a TSCF or NTSCF header a mixture of requests with and without presentation time in a single frame is not possible. A presentation time from a TSCF header will be applied to all ACFtypes within the frame."), TC18.txt L3622-3624

requirements.title: StreamFaultTracker is a bounded, multi-stream keyed wrapper that tracks each request stream's own independent CRC-fault latch
requirements.text: rcp::e2e::StreamFaultTracker::on_crc_error(stream_id, rx_enforce_e2e) shall apply a CRC_ERROR observed on stream_id to that stream's own independently-tracked RxStreamGuard (registering the stream on first touch if capacity remains, and returning false with no side effects only when stream_id is untracked and every one of its kMaxStreams slots is already in use); is_faulted(stream_id) shall report that stream's own latched state, vacuously false for a stream never seen; reset(stream_id) shall release only that stream's own latched fault, leaving every other tracked stream's state unaffected.
requirements.tc18: §12.7.7 Table 24 ("rx_enforce_e2e ... 1b: stream is blocked until released, when CRC check at EP fails. Safe state will be entered"), TC18.txt L2865-2867

requirements.title: RxSequenceGuard::evaluate enforces per-stream sequence-number admission (rx_enforce_seq) via RFC-1982 forward-distance comparison
requirements.text: rcp::e2e::RxSequenceGuard::evaluate shall accept every sequence number when RequestStreamConfig::rx_enforce_seq is clear, and shall set SeqResult::accept iff the received sequence number's modular forward distance from the last accepted value lies in [1, 127] when rx_enforce_seq is set -- an RFC-1982-style comparison that correctly handles the 8-bit AVTPDU sequence_num field's 0xFF->0x00 wraparound rather than a plain always-greater-than test.
